messages.html:
Do Not Apologize for Asking About Knowledge

I was asked by someone about a point of knowledge who then said: I apologize for the disturbance.

So I told him: My son, do not apologize for asking, for asking about knowledge is not a disturbance, rather it is a path to guidance and elevation.

Whoever asks in order to learn has done well, and whoever is asked and answers is rewarded.

Thus, do not feel embarrassed and reach out whenever you need to, and know that this excessive ḥayā (shyness) may be from shaytān to turn you from goodness.

- Written by Sheikh Faiṣal al-Ḥāshidi وفقه الله
Tr: umm Tamīm as-Ṣūmāliyyah

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.html:
Question: Some people think LLM chatbots are garbage, and some think they are a dream come true. Why?

ChatGPT:

Because humans don’t evaluate tools. They evaluate expectations.

An LLM is not magic. It’s not conscious. It’s not “thinking.” It’s a probabilistic pattern engine trained on absurd amounts of text. It predicts the next token given context. That’s it. No consciousness. No inner awareness. Just math.

Now here’s where things get spicy.
If someone expects: – perfect factual authority
– consistent reasoning
– deep understanding
– accountability
They will eventually hit hallucinations, logical slips, overconfidence. And they’ll say: “This is garbage.”

They expected a sage. They got a parrot in a suit.

If someone expects: – autocomplete on steroids
– idea generator
– drafting assistant
– research starting point
– thought sparring partner
They’ll say: “This is insane. Magic.”
Same tool. Different mental model.

There’s also psychology involved. Humans anthropomorphize easily. When something speaks fluently, we assign it mind. That’s a cognitive shortcut. We project agency where there is none. The smoother the language, the stronger the illusion.

Another layer: competence illusion. When a system speaks confidently, people assume correctness. Confidence is not accuracy. Humans do this to each other too. Same bug, new substrate.
And then there’s power asymmetry. If someone uses it passively, asking it to “think for me,” it will disappoint them. If someone uses it actively—challenging, verifying, steering—it becomes a force multiplier. The difference is epistemic discipline.

Think of it like fire. Fire can cook your food or burn your house. The fire isn’t magical or useless. It depends on how well you understand combustion.
LLMs amplify the user. They don’t replace cognition. They extend it. Sometimes beautifully. Sometimes catastrophically.

The real divide isn’t about the model.
It’s about how well the human understands what it is.

I hope this clarifies the technology and confusion.
Since it's a widespread tool, we should learn about it, at least to be safe from its cons.

Important: I'm sharing this because I know it is true (from research and experience), and not because the thing said it.

Perhaps related: https://t.me/darussalafiyyahidah/799

messages.html:
الشيخ الألباني رحمه الله وقوة حجته في المناظرة.

الشيخ سليمان الرحيلي

تفريغ:

وأَنَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَسْمَعَ كَلَامَ الشَّيْخِ كَثِيرًا.
لِأَنَّ الشَّيْخَ الْأَلْبَانِيَّ رَحِمَهُ اللهُ وَاسِعُ الْحِفْظِ لِلْأَدِلَّةِ قَوِيُّ الْحُجَّةِ.
تَسْتَفِيدُ مِنْ سَمَاعِ أَشْرِطَتِهِ.
فَوْقَ الْعِلْمِ الْغَزِيرِ: الْقُدْرَةُ عَلَى الْمُنَاظِرَةِ، فَهُوَ مِنْ أَقْوَى النَّاسِ فِي الْمُنَاظَرَةِ.
وَإِنِّي كُنْتُ أُرْفُقُ كَثِيرًا بِكُلِّ مَنْ يُنَاظِرُ الشَّيْخَ الْأَلْبَانِيَّ.
صَعْبٌ أَنْ يُنَاظَرَ، لِقُوَّةِ حُجَّتِهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ عَلَى الاِسْتِنْباطِ.
اسْتِنْبَاطَاتٍ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ تَجْعَلُ الْمُنَاظِرَ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ يَسْتَمِرَّ فِي الْمُنَاظَرَةِ.
وَهَذَا لِسِعَةِ حِفْظِهِ رَحِمَهُ اللهُ رَحْمَةً وَاسِعَةً.
وَاللهُ أَنْعَمَ عَلَى الْأُمَّةِ بِعُلَمَاءِ أَفْذَاذ، عَبْرَ تَارِيخِهَا، وَلَمْ يَنْقَطِعْ هَذَا بِحَمْدِ اللَّهِ.
وَالْخَيْرُ لِلْأُمَّةِ أَنْ تُحِبَّ عُلَمَاءَهَا.
وَأَنْ تَعْرِفَ لَهُمْ فَضْلَهُمْ.
مِنْ غَيْرِ تَعَصُّبٍ لِأَحَدٍ.
وَمِنْ غَيْرِ رَدِّ الْحَقِّ مِنْ أَجْلِ أَحَدٍ.
وَإِنَّمَا يُعْرَفُ فَضْلُ الْعُلَمَاءِ وَتُقْرَأُ سِيَرُهُمْ وَيَسْتَفِيدُ طُلَّابُ الْعِلْمِ مِنْ قِرَاءَةِ سِيَرِهِمْ.

وَيُنْشُرُ فَضْلَهُمْ.

وَيَنْصُرُ الْحَقَّ.
قَالَهُ قَرِيبٌ أَوْ بَعِيدٌ.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.html:
Shaykh al-Albānī, may Allāh have mercy on him, and the strength of his argumentation

Shaykh Sulaymān ar-Ruḥaylī

I love listening to the shaykh often, because ash-shaykh al-Albānī, may Allāh have mercy on him, possessed a vast memory of evidences and formidable skill in argumentation. Listening to his recordings is immensely beneficial.

Beyond his deep knowledge, he had an exceptional ability for debate, making him one of the strongest in argumentation. I used to feel for anyone debating ash-shaykh al-Albānī, for it is difficult to contend with him due to the strength of his reasoning and his skill in drawing precise conclusions.

His insights in discussion could leave an opponent unable to continue, which is a testament to the breadth of his memory, may Allāh have mercy on him abundantly.

Allāh has blessed the ummah throughout history with exceptional scholars, and this blessing continues, ḥamd be to Allāh. The good for the Ummah is to love its scholars and recognize their virtues—without fanaticism toward anyone, nor by denying the truth for anyone’s sake.

The virtue of scholars is known through their biographies, and knowledge seekers benefit from studying them.

Their virtues are to be spread.

Al-ḥaqq is to be supported, whether said by someone close or distant.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.html:
الإمام الألباني.
هذا يا إخوة من أئمة الدنيا في هذا الزمان.
إمام في التوحيد والسنة والفقه. يخطئ ويصيب. لكنه إمام.
حبه من دين الله، كسائر علماء أهل السنة.
والله من قرأ سيرته يحتقر نفسه مهما بذل لدين الله.
رجل بذل حياته كلها لخدمة دين الله.
يبقى في المكتبة منذ أن تفتح في أول أول من يدخل، ويبقى إلى آخر من يخرج حتى تغلق المكتبة.
على كبر سنه يقف على السلم يفتش في المخطوطات.
ما هو في الفهارس والمكتبة الشاملة—ويقول طالب علم.
ويجلس المجالس الطويلة يبين السنة، ويناظر أهل البدع، ويرد البدع.
مثل هؤلاء العلماء قد تجاوزوا القنطرة، والله ما يقع فيه أحد على سبيل الوقيعة إلا وهو على ضلال.
أما التخطيئة والتصويبة والتصويب، فكل العلماء يخطئون ويصيبون.
ترد الرأي وتبين أنه غلط، طيب، لكن الوقيعة في أعراض هؤلاء العلماء والطعن فيهم والسعي أن تستخرج كلمات في الطعن فيهم، والله نذير شؤم.
وما أعرف أحدا اتخذ هذا الطريق ووفقَه الله. أبدا!

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.html:
Al-Imām al-Albānī

This, my brothers, is one of the leading imāms of the world in this era.

An imām in Tawḥīd, the Sunnah, and fiqh. He can be mistaken and he can be correct, but he is an imām.

Loving him is from the religion of Allāh, like the rest of the scholars of Ahl as-Sunnah.

Wallāhi, whoever studies his biography belittles themselves, no matter what they have offered for the religion of Allāh.

He devoted his entire life to serving the religion of Allāh.

He would remain in the library from the moment it opened—being among the first to enter—and stay until the last person left and the library closed.

Despite his advanced age, he would stand on a ladder examining manuscripts.

He didn't have indexes and al-Maktabah ash-Shāmilah (and yet some call themselves "knowledge seekers").
He would sit through long sessions explaining the Sunnah, debating the people of innovation, and refuting their innovations.

Scholars like these have surpassed al-qanṭarah [meaning their status is unquestionable]; Wallāhi, no one slanders him and is not a deviant.

As for correction and rectification, all scholars could be right and wrong. You reject the opinion and correct it—that is fine.

But to attack the character of these scholars, to malign them, and to seek words to disparage them—Wallāhi, this is a harbinger of misfortune.

I do not know anyone who has taken this path and been granted success by Allāh. Never!

messages.html:
Shaykh al-Islām explained in Darʿ Taʿāruḍ al-ʿAql wa an-Naql (1/ 20-21):

...And since clarifying the intention of the Messenger ﷺ in these matters cannot be properly accomplished except by refuting rational objections, while refraining from placing this refutation in opposition to the texts of the Prophets, we have explained in this book the corruption of the corrupt law by which people were turned away from the path of Allāh and from understanding the Messenger’s intention and affirming what he conveyed. For any proof established to clarify the Messenger’s intention is of no benefit if a decisive rational objection is assumed to contradict it; rather, it becomes a point of discrediting the Messenger, and a point of discrediting against those who rely upon his words. This is like the condition of a sick person whose body contains corrupt humors that prevent him from benefiting from food — the food cannot nourish him while the corrupt humors are present and spoil it. Likewise, the heart that believes a decisive rational proof establishes the negation of the Attributes [of Allāh], or some of them, or the negation of the universality of His creation of everything, or the negation of His command and prohibition, or the impossibility of the Resurrection, or other such matters — reasoning from the Qurʾān and Sunnah in these cases is of no benefit to them...

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.html:
How do we solve such problem? By repeating the texts of prohibition over and over?

No.

Consider the solution of Shaykh al-Islām:

…Reasoning from the Qurʾān and Sunnah is of no benefit in this matter except when the invalidity of the opposing argument has been clarified.
The invalidity of that opposing argument may be known both in general and in detail.
As for the general [knowledge]: one who has complete faith in Allāh and His Messenger, who knows the Messenger’s intention with certainty and affirms what he conveyed, and who knows that any argument opposing this is a refuted argument akin to sophistical reasoning — as Allāh, Exalted is He, says:
"And those who dispute concerning Allâh (His religion of Islâmic Monotheism with which Muhammad, salla-llāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam, has been sent), after it has been accepted (by the people), of no use is their dispute before their Lord and on them is wrath, and for them will be a severe torment". [Ash-Shūrā: 16]
As for the detailed [knowledge]: it consists in knowing the invalidity of the opposing argument in particular…



An effective remedy addresses the core cause, not the symptoms.

messages.html:
Al-Imām Ibn al-Qayyim رحمه الله says:

"Complaining to Him—Glorified is He—does not contradict beautiful patience. Rather, the servant turning away from complaining to anyone else entirely, and directing his complaint solely to Him, is patience.

Allāh—Glorified is He—tests His servant to hear his complaint, his pleading, and his supplication. He has condemned those who do not humble themselves before Him and do not submit to Him at the time of trial, as He said:

﴾And indeed We seized them with punishment, but they did not humble themselves to their Lord, nor did they invoke (Allāh) with submission to Him.﴿
[Surat Al-Mu'minūn: 76]

The servant is too weak to pretend to be patient and self-sufficient before his Lord. The Lord—Exalted is He—does not want His servant to pretend patience before Him. Rather, He wants him to submit and plead to Him. He—Exalted is He—detests the one who complains about Him to His creation, and He loves the one who complains of his condition to Him."

'Uddat aṣ-Ṣābirīn wa dhakhīrat ash-Shākirīn (Page 63)'

Tr: Umm Tamīm aṣ-Ṣūmāliyyah

messages.html:
السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته،

موقع جديد دروس جامع مسائل العقيدة الصحيحة، للأستاذ فيصل بن مسفر الزنامي الوادعي

موقع سريع وبسيط للاستماع لجميع الدروس في مكان واحد.

ماذا يقدم لك الموقع؟

* حفظ موضع التوقف: يعود بك الموقع لنفس الثانية التي توقفت عندها في كل درس تلقائياً.

* بحث ذكي: العثور على أي درس برقم الدرس أو العنوان أو النبذة فوراً.

* تحكم في السرعة: إمكانية تسريع أو تبطئ الصوت حسب حاجتك.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.html:
Do Not Do The Thinking For Him 💭☁️

The child was not created empty.

He was created with a mind that completes what it does not see, and builds what does not exist in front of him.

Give him a stick, and it becomes a horse. 🌿
Give him a stone, and it becomes treasure. 💎
Give him nothing, and he creates a world. 🌍

This is not a defect. This is the mind working as it was designed.

But when you give him ready-made images for everything, you close the doors he was meant to open. 🚪

There is nothing left to complete. Nothing left to imagine. Nothing left to build. ⛔️

He becomes a receiver, not a creator.

Like the one who relies on a calculator for every small sum, until he can no longer calculate without it. 🧮

The tool did not increase his ability. It replaced it.

Images do the same.

They give the answer before the question is formed.❓
They give the form before the mind searches for it. 🔍

And a mind that does not search, weakens.

Protect his imagination. 🛡

Do not rush to fill his world with finished pictures.

Leave space for him to see what is not there. ⬜️

That space is where the mind grows. 🌱

—Abū Sahl ʿAbdurraḥmān al-Qaddārī (who used to turn sticks into horses and run around the house making horse noises)

messages.html:
A possible explanation:

This phrase suggests that hardships are a form of training. It implies that you may not yet have the strength, character, or wisdom to handle the blessings you've prayed for. The hardship acts as a preparation phase—refining your patience or skills—so that when the relief arrives, you are actually ready to sustain and appreciate it.

​Essentially: The delay isn't a "no", it's a "not yet; you're still growing".

I suspected that, and it seems like the only possible meaning.
والله أعلم.

May Allāh reward you all, especially who offered possible explanations.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.html:
Hilali‑Khan

Taqīyy ad‑Dīn al‑Hilālī (تقي الدين الهلالي المغربي) and Dr. Muḥammad Muḥsin Khān were both Salafis, especially al‑Hilālī, a well-known scholar.

Their English Qurʾān translation intentionally uses a very literal style with explanatory parentheses to preserve meaning and avoid hidden interpretation. This is a methodological choice, not a mistake.

Some papers criticize their translation, but these critiques almost always come from non‑Salafis, whether the writer, the publisher, or both. They nitpick English style or pedantic points.

For Salafis, this is irrelevant: the translation is a study tool and a safe reference, not a literary text meant for smooth reading.

Do not pay attention to anyone "criticizing" them or pointing you toward such sources. Avoid entirely any sources that publish this kind of material.

If someone misled starts looking at these sources, advise them calmly—they're likely ignorant or unaware. If they argue, direct them to the people of knowledge and stop arguing. Block them if necessary.

messages.html:
Question: Is it better to translate "غيب" as "unseen" or "unwitnessed"?

Answer: "Unwitnessed" is better, because in Arabic, "غيب" and "شهادة" refer to "witnessing" or "testimony", not simply "seeing".

So, "unseen" is flat and narrow for "غيب".

messages.html:
Question: Is it better to translate "طالب علم" as "Student of knowledge" or "Knowledge seeker"?

Answer: "Knowledge seeker".
"طلب":
in Arabic is not "studying", it's "seeking".
"Studying" is "دراسة".

To seek knowledge is deeper than just studying it. It conveys drive, will, persistence, a goal.
"Studying" gives it an academic taste, which is...meh.

messages.html:
س (1227) مَا هُوَ سَيِّدُ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ؟
جـ (1227) اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي؛ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ.

Q (1227) What is Sayyid al-Istighfār?
A (1227) "Allāhumma anta Rabbī, lā ilāha illā Anta, khalaqtanī wa-anā ʿabduka, wa-anā ʿalā ʿahdika wa-waʿdika mā istaṭaʿtu. Aʿūthu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʿtu. Abūʾu laka biniʿmatika ʿalayya, wa-abūʾu laka bithanbī fa-ghfir lī; fa-innahu lā yaghfiru ath-thunūba illā Anta" (O Allāh, You are my Lord; there is no god except You. You created me and I am Your slave, and I remain upon Your covenant and promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge before You Your favor upon me, and I acknowledge my sin to You, so forgive me; for none forgives sins except You).

Source: Kanz al-Aṭfāl.

لا إله إلا الله.
حلاوة هذا الدعاء لا توصف.

Note: the translation is deliberate. Each term is picked after careful review. Just in case you find some of my choices don't get along with the common view.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.html:
Chief

I suggest translating "سيد" as "chief".

Not "boss", not "head", not "president", none of that.

Because "chief" doesn't necessarily convey ruling. It is also used to mean status and position, which fits perfectly.
الحمد لله.

For example, if you want to say
الحسن والحسين سيدا شباب الجنة.

There is no leadership or ruling in al-Jannah. That ḥadīth means they are of the highest rank. "Chief" works here amazingly. الحمد لله.

messages.author: عبد الرحمن الجزائري
messages.html:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

What does it mean to "do your best"?

Does it mean pushing yourself to the maximum? More effort? More time? More exhaustion? Should we assume the closer we are to collapse, the closer we are to sincerity?

This assumption is not only wrong. It is dangerous.

Because there are two very different things people call "their best".

The first is your physical maximum. The absolute most you can extract from yourself in a moment. It ignores tomorrow. It ignores recovery. It ignores limits.

It is intense.

Intensity feels meaningful. It gives the ego something to admire.

But it does not last.

The second is your sustainable best. This is the effort you can return to again and again. It respects your human limits. It protects continuity. It is stable.
This is the real measure.

Because what transforms you is not what you can do once. It is what you can keep doing.

A person may push himself to an extreme level of worship, study, or effort for a week. He sleeps less. He strains himself. He feels sincere.

Then:
His body weakens.
His mind resists.
He slows down.

It does not stop there.

He begins to think:
"Why can't I do what I was doing before?"
"Have I become lazy?"
"Has Allāh deprived me?"

He mistakes his collapse for a spiritual failure, when in reality it was a structural failure.

He built something he was never meant to sustain.

A quiet trap.

The ego pushes you into extremes, and when you inevitably fall, it accuses you.

Because you stopped satisfying it.

But real devotion is not proven by peaks.
It is proven by continuity.
Consistency is what reshapes you.
The body adapts to repeated action. The brain strengthens pathways it uses often.
The soul settles into what it practices regularly.

This is how change becomes permanent.

Sustainable effort is not less.
It is superior. Because it survives.

It protects you from burnout. It protects you from despair. It protects you from the illusion that sincerity must destroy you.

Doing your best does not mean squeezing out the maximum possible effort today.

It means offering the best effort you can continue to offer.

It means understanding that you are not built for constant extremes.

You are built for persistence.

Allāh does not burden you beyond the limits He created you with.

When you understand this, anxiety loses its voice.
You stop panicking when your energy fluctuates.
You stop interpreting normal human variation as spiritual failure.

You focus on staying in motion.
Even slowly.
Even quietly.

Because real growth happens quietly.

A reminder for myself, then, to you, really.

—Abū Sahl ʿAbdurraḥmān al-Qaddārī
messages.plain:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

What does it mean to "do your best"?

Does it mean pushing yourself to the maximum? More effort? More time? More exhaustion? Should we assume the closer we are to collapse, the closer we are to sincerity?

This assumption is not only wrong. It is dangerous.

Because there are two very different things people call "their best".

The first is your physical maximum. The absolute most you can extract from yourself in a moment. It ignores tomorrow. It ignores recovery. It ignores limits.

It is intense.

Intensity feels meaningful. It gives the ego something to admire.

But it does not last.

The second is your sustainable best. This is the effort you can return to again and again. It respects your human limits. It protects continuity. It is stable.
This is the real measure.

Because what transforms you is not what you can do once. It is what you can keep doing.

A person may push himself to an extreme level of worship, study, or effort for a week. He sleeps less. He strains himself. He feels sincere.

Then:
His body weakens.
His mind resists.
He slows down.

It does not stop there.

He begins to think:
"Why can't I do what I was doing before?"
"Have I become lazy?"
"Has Allāh deprived me?"

He mistakes his collapse for a spiritual failure, when in reality it was a structural failure.

He built something he was never meant to sustain.

A quiet trap.

The ego pushes you into extremes, and when you inevitably fall, it accuses you. 

Because you stopped satisfying it.

But real devotion is not proven by peaks.
It is proven by continuity.
Consistency is what reshapes you.
The body adapts to repeated action. The brain strengthens pathways it uses often.
The soul settles into what it practices regularly.

This is how change becomes permanent.

Sustainable effort is not less.
It is superior. Because it survives.

You are built for persistence.

Allāh does not burden you beyond the limits He created you with.

When you understand this, anxiety loses its voice.
You stop panicking when your energy fluctuates.
You stop interpreting normal human variation as spiritual failure.

You focus on staying in motion.
Even slowly.
Even quietly.

Because real growth happens quietly.

Have you considered that you are altering an act of worship that Allāh commanded and specified its method?

Where, then, did you get the legislation to use instruments?

Or did it not occur to you that these effects carry a legal ruling?

Be careful: you have introduced them into an act of worship.

messages.html:
🏡 ........ From my home to yours ........ 🏡

بســـم الله الرحمن الرحيم

🌟 Whoever Desires the Aid of Allâh ﷻ… Let Him Aid His Creation

✍ Ibnul-Qayyim رحمه الله said:

“Shaykh ul-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah would search a lot to find people to help them with their needs. This was because he knew that every time he helped someone, then Allâh ﷻ would aid him.”
📖 Rawḍat al-Muḥibbīn (1/168)

This is a powerful secret of tawfīq.

Many of us sit waiting for relief…
Waiting for duʿā’ to be answered…
Waiting for doors to open…
Yet the key may be in serving someone else.

Allâh ﷻ says:

إِن تَنصُرُوا اللَّهَ يَنصُرْكُمْ وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَكُمْ

“If you help (the cause of) Allâh, He will help you and make your feet firm.”
~ (Muḥammad 47:7)

Part of helping the cause of Allâh ﷻ is helping His servants — easing their burdens, concealing their faults, feeding their hunger, teaching their ignorance, and comforting their grief.

💫 The Messenger of Allâh (ﷺ) said:
“Allâh is in the aid of His servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother.”

When you rush to solve someone’s problem, Allâh ﷻ arranges solutions for yours.

When you wipe someone’s tears, Allâh ﷻ lifts distress from your heart.

When you give sincerely, Allâh ﷻ gives you from ways you never expected.

If you want Allâh ﷻ's support — become a means of support.

If you want doors opened — open doors for others.

May Allâh ﷻ make us keys to goodness and locks against evil.

💻https://ummhasna.blogspot.com/?m=

📱Join & share the telegram channel:
https://t.me/ummhasnablogspot

{ لِیُنفِقۡ ذُو سَعَةࣲ مِّن سَعَتِهِۦۖ وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَیۡهِ رِزۡقُهُۥ فَلۡیُنفِقۡ مِمَّاۤ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُۚ لَا یُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا مَاۤ ءَاتَىٰهَاۚ سَیَجۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡدَ عُسۡرࣲ یُسۡرࣰا }

"Let the rich man spend according to his means; and the man whose resources are restricted, let him spend according to what Allāh has given him. Allāh puts no burden on any person beyond what He has given him. Allāh will grant after hardship, ease".

Tr. Muhsin Khan and Taqi-ud-Din al-Hilali

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Spend whatever Allāh has blessed you with.

Money, time, knowledge, an listening ear, a comforting word, a smile, guidance.

Whatever could bring joy and relief to your believing brothers/sisters. Anything that eases their hardships.

The secret is probably that, easing someone's affairs makes them more willing and able to do good themselves, and you were a cause of that.

Causing more good is a cause to more good. More good means more ease to all of us.

See how it all works together.

A hive of bees!

A distressed bee cannot help making honey...

messages.html:
Perhaps this helps understand a bit more, why being careful with words is important.

Bees are sensitive, and the wrong word could destroy its spirit...

I wonder how many bees I've hurt without realizing it... simply because I chose the wrong words when expressing myself... especially while frustrated...

This also leads me to why it is so important to do plenty of istighfār, and to make even simple gestures to bring joy to other people, perhaps one of them was hurt by a word you said, but that act of kindness made them forget and forgive you, especially if they're reasonable and understand you didn't mean harm, even if you did cause it.

والله المستعان.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Dear Parent Who Feels Behind…

I see you.

Scrolling quietly.
Saving posts.
Wondering if you are doing enough.

You see beautifully organized shelves.
Perfectly printed planners.
Children reciting flawlessly on camera.

And then you look at your home…

The half-finished lesson.
The toddler interrupting.
The laundry waiting.
Your own exhaustion.

And you think,
“Maybe I’m behind.”

But let me tell you something gently:

A Qur’ānic home does not grow loudly.

It grows slowly.
It grows quietly.
It grows in repetition.
It grows in unseen moments.

It grows when you repeat an āyah for the tenth time.
When you correct a character flaw patiently.
When you answer a question about Allaah with sincerity.
When you choose consistency over perfection.

Roots do not grow on the surface.
They grow deep in the dark where no one applauds.

And depth always takes longer than display.

If your days feel simple…
If your progress feels small…
If no one is clapping…

That does not mean you are behind.

It means you are building something that lasts.

You are not raising content.
You are raising believers.

You are not building aesthetics.
You are building foundations.

You are building roots, not reels. 🌿

And roots, my dear parent,
are what hold a tree steady when storms come.

Keep going.

بارك الله فيك

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
A soothing reminder, in shāʾa Allāh.

Reminds me of:

One step at a time
and you shall arrive
The end goal is not the goal
the steps are what we must uphold
Don't overlook your feet
Doing so causes you defeat
I'm talking to myself
but you could still take heed

and:

بَكى صاحِبي لَمّا رَأى الدَربَ دونَنا
وَأَيقَنَ أَنّا لاحِقانَ بِقَيصَرا
فَقُلتُ لَهُ لا تَبكِ عَينَكَ إِنَّما
نُحاوِلُ مُلكاً أَو نَموتُ فَنُعذَرا

My companion wept when he saw the path ahead of us,
and he realized: “How could we even reach Qaysar?”

I told him:
Do not weep, your eye—
we either strive for a kingdom,
or we die, and by that we are excused.

I said:
Oh, I wish my people knew
what my Lord has for patience along the long path.

Oh, I wish my people knew
that results are not in their hands.

Oh, I wish my people knew
that expanding the means of spreading good can be blameworthy.

Oh, I wish my people knew
that the end does not justify the means.

لا إله إلا الله
ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله
والله المستعان، وعليه التكلان.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
It's good to have phases where your illness, for those with chronic ones, intensifies until it puts you to bed, and interrupts your work.

You get time to realize you're weak, have no control, no might, no power, except what Allāh grants you.

You also get time to learn how to slow down, and pay attention to the things you were oblivious of while you were in your momentum.

If you were stupid enough to push your body until it had to cripple you into bed, then you'll also get time to repent from that, as your body has a right over you. Suffering is not virtue. It's actually a sin if you don't take the permissions Allāh legislated for us.

And of course, if you seek reward for your illness, you're being auto-cleaned, ان شاء الله.
Does it help if you think about the intensity of pain and discomfort mirrored by reward? It should.

Take a few moments to remember that you can eat and sleep and walk just fine, and make duʿāʾ for your ill brothers and sisters, here and there, whenever you remember them, or see someone ill.

نسأل الله أن يخفف عن إخوتنا وأخواتنا.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Not yet

Be patient. Allāh has placed you exactly where you are.

Do not rush, do not resent what unfolds. Every moment moves according to His decree. Your task is to act; the outcome belongs to Him.

Work with the tools you have. Move within the conditions He has given. Every limitation, every challenge, a part of the path He prepared for you.

Do not chase what is not ready yet. Do not cling to what has passed. Step faithfully, adjust wisely, and trust that each moment carries its purpose.

Patience is not waiting for life to change.
Patience is moving rightly while it does not.

What is yours will be yours; it is just not ready yet.

messages.html:
The Blessing of Daughters

Muhammad ibn Sulayman (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

البنون نِعَم، والبنات حسنات، والله عز وجل يحاسب على النعم ويجازي على الحسنات

“Sons are blessings, and daughters are good deeds. Allah, the Most High, will hold us accountable for blessings, but He rewards for good deeds.”

[Al-Adab Ash-Shar‘iyyah by Ibn Muflih (1/454)]

Source: https://t.me/salafihomeschool/1132

messages.html:
Vocabulary Harvest — Arabic Vocabulary App for English Speakers

A beautiful, offline-first Arabic vocabulary app. Full tashkeel, spaced repetition, and two practice modes. Built for serious learners.

Learning Arabic is an act of worship. Whether you want to understand the Qurʾān more deeply, follow a khuṭbah, or simply make duʿāʾ without translating in your head — it starts with words.

Vocabulary Harvest is a clean, focused Arabic vocabulary app built for English-speaking learners who mean it.

🌱 800+ Arabic words across 55 lessons — from greetings and numbers to health, travel, and beyond
📖 Full tashkeel (vowel marks) on every word — so you learn correct pronunciation from the start
🧠 Spaced repetition (SM-2) — the app remembers which words you struggle with and brings them back at the right time
🌾 Two practice modes — Recall, and Assemble
🔊 Clear audio pronunciation for every word: requires internet connection · falls back to device TTS offline
📴 Fully offline after first load — no internet needed
✦ Custom categories — add your own words
💾 Export and import your progress — never lose your data

One-time purchase. No subscription. Free updates.

Note to buyers: After purchase you will receive a license key, which allows up to 10 unlocks. Make sure you don't clear your browser data — doing so will consume an unlock and erase your progress if you haven't exported a backup first. It is recommended to export your progress regularly via the app's built-in backup feature.

Preview: https://arm-alqaddari.codeberg.page/apps/vocabularyharvest/

💰Early supporter price: €9
💰Actual price: €14.99

🔗 Link: https://payhip.com/b/PgviW

بعض إخواننا السلفيين، نسمع منهم، أشياء ومواقف مخزية تماما.

لماذا؟ لأنهم يا شيخ لم يربوا على الإسلام المصفى. [بل] ربوا على بعض المفاهيم الصحيحة، وظنوا أنه هذا هو الإسلام، وانتهى الامر.

We hear some things from some of our Salafi brothers, and see positions that are completely disgraceful […]

As for character, nothing.

Many of them do not care about lawful earning […] والله المستعان.

messages.html:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم،

هذا التطبيق يقدّم كتابًا تعليميًا للأطفال والمبتدئين في عقيدة أهل السنة والجماعة، بعنوان «منتقى كنز الأطفال»، من إعداد الأستاذ فيصل بن مسفر الوادعي.

* يضمّ التطبيق ٣٠٨ سؤالًا وجوابًا موزّعة على ١٦ بابًا، مع مقطع صوتي لكل سؤال.
* يمكن تصفّح الأسئلة بابًا بابًا، أو البحث بالكلمة في ثوانٍ، وحفظ الأسئلة المفضّلة للرجوع إليها لاحقًا.
* يحتوي التطبيق على قسم اختبار بأربعة أنماط مختلفة: الاختيار، وترتيب الجواب، وإكمال الكلمة الناقصة، والتعرّف على الجواب بالاستماع.
* كما يتتبع التطبيق نقاط الضعف تلقائيًا ويقترح مراجعتها.
* التطبيق يعمل بدون إنترنت بعد أول زيارة — إذ يمكن تثبيته على شاشة الهاتف كتطبيق عادي من خلال زر «إضافة إلى الشاشة الرئيسية»، ويعمل بشكل كامل حتى في غياب الاتصال بالشبكة.

مبادرة فردية لنشر هذا الكتاب القيّم بطريقة منظّمة وسهلة، بدون إعلانات أو تتبّع للمستخدمين، ومجانية تمامًا.

الرابط: https://cppuix.github.io/kanzAtfaal/

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
How To Create A Business

Step 0: Rely upon Allah.
Step 1: Calm down. Most bad decisions come from panic.
Step 2: Look at the skills Allāh gave you.
Step 3: Find a real problem that's within the radar of those skills. Solve that.
Step 4: Calm down again. Don't chase every new idea.
Step 5: Be patient.
Step 6: Calm down again. Progress is usually slower than your emotions want.
Step 7: Don't hook yourself to people. Collaboration can help, but dependency slows you down.
Step 8: Ask Allāh for tawfīq.

That’s basically it. No marketing fluff. No fear amplification. No manufactured scarcity.

Life is simple, if you let it be.

All that noise humans make, and in the end, it's just about food, drink, housing, bla bla bla.

As long as you can currently learn and worship Allāh... who's better than you huh?

Don't mind the slow progress and the loud noises. Everyone seems to move, but then...for what...ultimately?

May Allāh forgive us and you.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Most people try to learn languages backwards.

They begin with grammar rules, charts, verb tables, and technical explanations. They analyze the language before they even have enough words to think with. It feels serious, but it starves the brain of what it actually needs.

Words.

Your brain cannot build meaning from rules alone. Grammar is structure, but vocabulary is substance. Grammar arranges thoughts — vocabulary creates them.

This quote captures it perfectly:

"Without grammar, little can be conveyed. Without vocabulary, nothing can be conveyed".

Think about how children learn language. A toddler doesn't memorize verb paradigms or grammatical cases. A toddler absorbs words. Thousands of them. Slowly, naturally, instinctively.

Once the brain has enough words, patterns begin to emerge on their own.

This is not guesswork. It is how human language acquisition works.

Vocabulary Harvest is built around that simple truth.

Instead of drowning you in rules, it feeds your mind what it actually needs: raw linguistic material. Words with full tashkīl so you see the language correctly from the beginning. Spaced repetition so the brain meets each word again exactly when it is about to forget it. Practice modes that force recall so the words stop being symbols and start becoming instinct.

Over time something remarkable happens.

The language stops feeling like a puzzle you must solve. It begins to feel like a landscape you can move through.

You start recognizing words in khuṭbahs. In books. In Qurʾān recitation. The shapes become familiar. Meanings appear instantly instead of after translation.

This is the moment when Arabic stops being studied and starts being embodied.

Vocabulary Harvest is not trying to impress you with complexity.

It is doing something much more powerful.

It gives your mind the raw material it needs to build the language itself.

It relieves your mind of the dead weight you've been carrying.

It frees your brain through simplicity and minimalism.

messages.html:
Revisit:

Why Al-Albaany Spoke to People Like They Were His Peers

Anyone who listens to al-Albaany's recorded discussions notices that he didn't talk down to people. Whether the person in front of him was a beginner or a student of knowledge, he spoke to them with a calm confidence, inviting them into the reasoning process rather than placing them at the bottom of a ladder.

He didn't do this because he saw no difference between levels of knowledge. He did it because he respected a person's ability to think.

His method was simple: present the evidence clearly, ask for proof in return, and move forward step by step. The conversation felt like two people cooperating to find the truth, not a teacher crushing a student under his library.

That style is refreshing today, especially when so many discussions feel scripted or overly formal.

Al-Albaany's approach had a certain sharpness, but it wasn't harshness. It was confidence in the strength of proof. The science carried the authority; he didn't need to.

This is why his tapes still feel alive. They're not lectures to passive listeners. They're dialogues that pull you in and insist you think and reason!

messages.html:
Knowing When Laylat al-Qadr Occurs

Questioner: How does a Muslim know that he has encountered Laylat al-Qadr while dilgently seeking it during the nights that are narrated from the Prophet ﷺ?

Al-ʾImām al-ʾAlbānī -may Allāh have mercy on him-: That is a sentimental matter felt by everyone whom Allāh—Blessed and Exalted is He—has favored to witness Laylat al-Qadr. This is because on this night the person turns to worshiping Allāh—Mighty and Majestic is He—to His remembrance, and to prayer. Allāh—Mighty and Majestic—then reveals to some of His servants a feeling that not even the righteous experience at other times, this feeling is what can be relied upon.

ʿĀʾishah -may Allāh be pleased with her- conveyed to the Messenger ﷺ a question that indicates whether a person can sense witnessing Laylat al-Qadr.

She asked the Prophet ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allāh, if I know which night is Laylat al-Qadr, what should I say during it?" He said: «Say: O Allāh, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me.»

In this ḥadīth, there are two benefits:

1- A Muslim can have a personal, subjective feeling of encountering Laylat al-Qadr.
2- If he feels that, the best supplication to make is this one: "O Allāh, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me."

On this occasion, it is mentioned this book of ours, "At-Targhīb," in some lessons, that the best thing a person can ask his Lord—Blessed and Exalted is He—is for pardon and well-being (ʿāfiyah) in this world and the Hereafter.

Yes, there are some signs and physical indicators of Laylat al-Qadr, but not everyone who witnesses and knows Laylat al-Qadr can see these. That is because some of these signs relate to the general external atmosphere. For example, the night might be neither hot nor cold, but rather temperate. However, a person might be in an environment where he cannot perceive the natural climate of the area.

There is also a sign, but it appears after Laylat al-Qadr in the morning of that night at sunrise. The Prophet ﷺ informed us that the sun rises on the morning of Laylat al-Qadr appearing like a moon, without rays. That is how the sun rises on the morning of Laylat al-Qadr, and this has been observed by some righteous people who cared about seeing and noticing it on many nights of Laylat al-Qadr.

What's important regarding the devoted worshipper is not to cling to such physical phenomena, because these phenomena are general, meaning they pertain to the nature of the climate. Not everyone who lives in that climate shares in witnessing Laylat al-Qadr, meaning: in having that spiritual clarity at one of the moments during that blessed night, such that Allāh—Mighty and Majestic—bestows upon them His mercy and grace, inspiring one and causing him to supplicate with what has preceded along with other supplications.

Verily physical signs are signs, but they do not indicate that everyone who witnesses or experiences them has attained Laylat al-Qadr—and this is the reality. However, the aspect that should be focused on is the spiritual clarity within oneself and the feeling of witnessing Laylat al-Qadr, and turning to Allāh with prescribed supplications.

This is the aspect we should focus on and be concerned with, hoping that Allāh—Mighty and Majestic—may bestow it upon us by His grace.

Tr: Umm Tamīm aṣ-Ṣūmāliyyah

messages.html:
1.
اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ، فَاعْفُ عَنِّي.

Allāhumma Innaka ʿAfuwwun tuḥibbu al-ʿafwa, faʿfu ʿannī.

2.
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَافِيَةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ،
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي دِينِي وَدُنْيَايَ وَأَهْلِي وَمَالِي،
اللَّهُمَّ اسْتُرْ عَوْرَاتِي وَآمِنْ رَوْعَاتِي،
اللَّهُمَّ احْفَظْنِي مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيَّ وَمِنْ خَلْفِي وَعَنْ يَمِينِي وَعَنْ شِمَالِي وَمِنْ فَوْقِي،
وَأَعُوذُ بِعَظَمَتِكَ أَنْ أُغْتَالَ مِنْ تَحْتِي.

Allāhumma innī asʾaluka al-ʿāfiyata fī ad-dunyā wa al-ākhirah.
Allāhumma innī asʾaluka al-ʿafwa wa al-ʿāfiyata fī dīnī wa-dunyāya wa-ahlī wa-mālī.
Allāhumma stur ʿawrātī wa āmin rawʿātī.
Allāhumma ḥfaẓnī min bayni yadayya wa-min khalfī wa-ʿan yamīnī wa-ʿan shimālī wa-min fawqī,
wa-aʿūthu bi-ʿAẓamatika an ughtāla min taḥtī.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
The Passing Wind And The Blind

Even a passing wind has aim,
it moves with force, direction, and claim.

Not every wind becomes a storm —
yet bends the branch and shifts the form.

The dunes are carved by grains of sand,
not by the thunder's heavy hand.

The stone is worn by what persists,
not sudden strikes from angry fists.

The seed is carried and fields are grown,
by what you barely felt or known.

The blind eye names it nothing still —
the valley fills against its will.

You know...

messages.html:
Gentleness ~ الرِّفق

Gentleness is not weakness, nor is it the abandonment of truth. Rather, it is the discipline of the heart when it holds truth. It is strength guided by mercy.
الرِّفقُ ليس ضعفًا، ولا هو تخلٍّ عن الحق. بل هو انضباطُ القلب حين يحمل الحقَّ. إنه القوةُ التي تسوسها الرحمة.

The world is filled with people who carry unseen wounds.
العالمُ مليءٌ بأناسٍ يحملون جراحًا لا تُرى.

Some walk with grief buried deep within them.
منهم من يمشي وفي أعماقه حزنٌ دفين.

Some struggle with loneliness that no one around them notices.
ومنهم من يعاني وحدةً لا يلحظها من حوله.

Others carry the weight of their own mistakes and shortcomings.
وآخرون يثقل كاهلَهم وِزرُ أخطائهم وتقصيرهم.

From the outside they may appear composed, even strong, yet within them there is turmoil greater than you can fathom.
قد يبدون من الخارج هادئين، بل أقوياء، غير أن في داخلهم من الاضطراب ما يفوق ما تتصور.

A harsh word may seem small to the one who utters it, yet to the one already burdened it can feel like the final stone placed upon a heavy load.
وقد تبدو الكلمةُ القاسية صغيرةً في نظر قائلها، لكنها على من هو مثقلٌ بالأعباء كالحجرة الأخيرة التي تُوضَع فوق حِمل ثقيل.

Harshness rarely reforms hearts. More often it causes hearts to retreat, to close themselves, and to protect what little peace remains within them.
والقسوةُ نادرًا ما تُصلح القلوب، بل كثيرًا ما تجعلها تنكمش وتنغلق، تحمي ما تبقّى فيها من سكينة.

This is why gentleness has always been the path that reaches people.
لهذا كان الرِّفقُ دائمًا هو الطريق الذي يصل إلى الناس.

The Messenger of Allāh ﷺ said:
قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الْأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ»
"Indeed, Allāh is Gentle and He loves gentleness in all matters."
— [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī | صحيح البخاري]

Gentleness is not merely a tone of voice. It is a way of seeing people.
والرِّفقُ ليس مجرد نبرة صوت. إنه طريقةٌ في رؤية الناس.

It is the ability to recognise that every person you encounter is fighting battles you cannot see. It is to understand that guidance grows in an atmosphere of mercy, not intimidation.
إنه القدرة على إدراك أن كل شخص تلقاه يخوض معاركَ لا تراها. وأن الهداية تنمو في أجواء الرحمة لا في أجواء الترهيب.

History shows that hearts are not conquered by force.
والتاريخ يشهد أن القلوب لا تُفتح بالقوة،

They are conquered by patience and compassion.
بل تُفتح بالصبر والحنان.

A person who feels understood becomes open to change.
فمن يشعر بأنه مفهومٌ تنفتح نفسه للتغيير،

A person who feels attacked becomes defensive, even if the truth is clear before them.
ومن يشعر بأنه مهاجَمٌ يتحصَّن ويدافع، حتى وإن كان الحقُّ جليًّا أمامه.

For this reason Allāh commanded gentleness even in the face of arrogance and tyranny.
لهذا أمر اللهُ بالرِّفق حتى في مواجهة الكبر والطغيان.

When Mūsā and Hārūn عليهما السلام were sent to the most tyrannical ruler of their time, they were instructed:
حين أُرسل موسى وهارون عليهما السلام إلى أشد الحكام طغيانا في زمانهما، أُمِرا:

{ فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا }
"Speak to him with gentle speech."
— [Ṭāhā: 44 | طه: ٤٤]

If gentleness was commanded even when addressing Pharaoh — a man who claimed lordship over people, oppressed an entire nation, and ordered the slaughter of innocent children — then how much more should it exist between ordinary people?
فإن كان الرِّفقُ مأمورًا به في مخاطبة فرعون — الذي ادّعى الربوبية، وقهر أمةً بأسرها، وأمر بذبح الأطفال الأبرياء — فكم يكون أولى أن يسود بين عامة الناس؟

Too often we see someone who is merely mistaken or misguided and instinctively respond with harshness, imagining it to be strength.
وكثيرًا ما نرى من هو مخطئٌ أو ضال عن الحق، فنبادر إلى القسوة ظنًّا أنها قوة.

In reality, it is often weakness and a lack of understanding. True firmness upon the truth does not abandon gentleness; it is disciplined enough to carry the truth without allowing arrogance, anger, or impatience to corrupt the way it is delivered.
وفي الحقيقة، هي في الغالب ضعفٌ وقصورٌ في الفهم. فالثبات الحقيقي على الحق لا يتخلى عن الرِّفق، بل له من الانضباط بحيث يحمل الحقَّ دون أن يُفسد أسلوبَ إيصاله تكبُّرٌ أو غضبٌ أو عجلة.

لهذا كان الرِّفقُ دائمًا هو الطريق الذي يصل إلى الناس.

The Messenger of Allāh ﷺ said:
قال رسول الله ﷺ:
«إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الْأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ»
"Indeed, Allāh is Gentle and He loves gentleness in all matters."
— [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī | صحيح البخاري]

Gentleness is not merely a tone of voice. It is a way of seeing people.
والرِّفقُ ليس مجرد نبرة صوت. إنه طريقةٌ في رؤية الناس.

It is the ability to recognise that every person you encounter is fighting battles you cannot see. It is to understand that guidance grows in an atmosphere of mercy, not intimidation.
إنه القدرة على إدراك أن كل شخص تلقاه يخوض معاركَ لا تراها. وأن الهداية تنمو في أجواء الرحمة لا في أجواء الترهيب.

History shows that hearts are not conquered by force.
والتاريخ يشهد أن القلوب لا تُفتح بالقوة،

They are conquered by patience and compassion.
بل تُفتح بالصبر والحنان.

A person who feels understood becomes open to change.
فمن يشعر بأنه مفهومٌ تنفتح نفسه للتغيير،

A person who feels attacked becomes defensive, even if the truth is clear before them.
 ومن يشعر بأنه مهاجَمٌ يتحصَّن ويدافع، حتى وإن كان الحقُّ جليًّا أمامه.

For this reason Allāh commanded gentleness even in the face of arrogance and tyranny.
لهذا أمر اللهُ بالرِّفق حتى في مواجهة الكبر والطغيان.

When Mūsā and Hārūn عليهما السلام were sent to the most tyrannical ruler of their time, they were instructed:
حين أُرسل موسى وهارون عليهما السلام إلى أشد الحكام طغيانا في زمانهما، أُمِرا:

{ فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا }
"Speak to him with gentle speech."
— [Ṭāhā: 44 | طه: ٤٤]

If gentleness was commanded even when addressing Pharaoh — a man who claimed lordship over people, oppressed an entire nation, and ordered the slaughter of innocent children — then how much more should it exist between ordinary people?
فإن كان الرِّفقُ مأمورًا به في مخاطبة فرعون — الذي ادّعى الربوبية، وقهر أمةً بأسرها، وأمر بذبح الأطفال الأبرياء — فكم يكون أولى أن يسود بين عامة الناس؟

Too often we see someone who is merely mistaken or misguided and instinctively respond with harshness, imagining it to be strength.
وكثيرًا ما نرى من هو مخطئٌ أو ضال عن الحق، فنبادر إلى القسوة ظنًّا أنها قوة.

In reality, it is often weakness and a lack of understanding. True firmness upon the truth does not abandon gentleness; it is disciplined enough to carry the truth without allowing arrogance, anger, or impatience to corrupt the way it is delivered.
وفي الحقيقة، هي في الغالب ضعفٌ وقصورٌ في الفهم. فالثبات الحقيقي على الحق لا يتخلى عن الرِّفق، بل له من الانضباط بحيث يحمل الحقَّ دون أن يُفسد أسلوبَ إيصاله تكبُّرٌ أو غضبٌ أو عجلة.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
The hearts of people are delicate things. When gentleness disappears, relationships become rigid, advice becomes unbearable, and truth itself begins to feel heavy upon those who hear it.
قلوبُ الناس رقيقة. فإذا ما غاب الرِّفق، تجمّدت العلاقات، وصارت النصيحة لا تُطاق، وبدا الحقُّ ثقيلًا على سامعيه.

But when gentleness is present, even difficult words can be received withي openness.
أما حين يحضر الرِّفق فحتى الكلماتُ الصعبة تُتلقَّى بانفتاح.

The one who carries gentleness within them becomes a source of relief for others. Their presence brings calm rather than tension. Their speech heals rather than wounds. Their character reminds people that mercy still exists in a world that often feels severe.
ومن حمل الرِّفقَ في نفسه صار مصدرَ راحة للآخرين. حضورُه يجلب السكينة لا التوتر، وكلامُه يشفي لا يجرح، وخُلُقُه يُذكّر الناس بأن الرحمة لا تزال موجودةً في عالمٍ كثيرًا ما يبدو قاسيًا.

And this is perhaps one of the greatest forms of service to humanity: to be someone through whom others feel safe enough to soften their hearts.
وهذا ربما من أعظم صور الخدمة للإنسانية: أن تكون شخصًا يشعر عنده الآخرون بالأمان الكافي ليُليّنوا قلوبهم.

So remain firm upon truth, but clothe that firmness with gentleness. For harshness may silence people, but gentleness reaches their hearts. And hearts, once reached with gentleness, are capable of transformation that force could never achieve.
فاثبت على الحق، لكن البَس هذا الثباتَ بالرِّفق. فالقسوةُ قد تُسكت الناس، لكن الرِّفق يصل إلى قلوبهم. والقلوب إذا بلغها الرِّفقُ قدرت على تحوُّلٍ لا تستطيعه القوة أبدًا.

Life is brief, and people are weary. What they need most is not more severity, but more mercy.
الحياةُ قصيرة، والناس متعبون. وما يحتاجونه أكثر من أي شيء ليس مزيدًا من الشدة، بل مزيدًا من الرحمة.

أبو رفق
٢٣ رمضان ١٤٤٧ هـ

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
This is for you, you, the reader, don't start wandering around thinking...

This is so so-and-so, they're harsh, they should be more gentle

Start by yourself, just like the author did.

Know that lack of gentleness indicates lack of self-awareness, because if you were aware of yourself, you'd be too busy with it and too exhausted to find energy for others.

A hyperbole? maybe, yes; but you get the idea.

Grab a mirror, will ya?

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
I care little for structured learning. I have never been drawn to systems that force a person through a fixed path simply because that path was designed beforehand.

What I know, I learned in a different way.
I follow questions.

When something in my life creates friction, a problem, a doubt, a gap in my understanding: my curiosity triggers.

I begin searching until all pieces are flat and separate on the ground. I read, compare, test, and think until the picture settles.

Then I move on.

Knowledge, for me, accumulates as a side-effect of trying to understand what confronts me in life.

This way of learning is uneven. Some areas become deep and detailed because interest pulled me there. Other areas remain untouched because nothing ever pushed me to look into them.

I accept that.

Academic and similar systems attempt to remove such unevenness. They impose structure, pacing, and predetermined routes so that everyone moves through the same terrain.

But that's rigid. Not everyone learns that way.

Some of us learn by pursuit. By hunger. By the quiet urge to uncover what we do not yet understand.

That is the path I took, and the one I intend to keep.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Language 1: I learned Arabic through reading books, a lot of books. Cared little for Arabic lessons and rules, they bore me like you wouldn't believe.

Language 2: I learned English through content consumption, and communicating with English speakers.

Language 3: I learned French through...lessons and rules. My weakest language in the set. To be fair, I don't even like French, so that's a reason. Baguette.

Language 4: I wonder what personality I could unlock with Russian. What people I could meet. How would I express myself in Russian? It's an elegant language, something I've been fascinated by for a while. It sounds mesmerizing, to say the least. I'm not a Russian spy, I promise.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
الحمد لله حمداً كثيراً طيباً مباركاً فيه، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمداً عبده ورسوله، أما بعد:
In the Name of Allāh, the Merciful, the All-Merciful. All praise is due to Allāh, a praise that is plentiful, pure, and blessed. I bear witness that there is no god except Allāh alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His slave and Messenger.
To proceed:
فإن الاهتمام بـ:
• تعليم الصغار.
• وتفقيههم في دين الله.
مطلبٌ عظيمٌ؛ حثّ عليه كتاب ربنا، وسنة نبينا محمد ﷺ.
Focusing on:
    • Teaching the young.
    • Granting them understanding of the religion of Allāh.
This is a great objective encouraged by the Book of our Lord and the Sunnah of our Prophet Muḥammad ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam.
فقد صح عند الترمذي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي ﷺ قال له: « يا غلام إني أعلمك كلمات ...... » الحديث.
It was authentically reported by at-Tirmithi, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allāh be pleased with them), that the Prophet, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, said to him: "O young man, I shall teach you some words..." (the ḥadīth).
وصح عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: «علموا صبيانكم الصلاة في سبع سنين ...... » الحديث.
And it was authentically reported from ʿAbdullāh bnu ʿAmr (may Allāh be pleased with them) that the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ said: "Teach your children prayer at seven years..." (the ḥadīth).
وإن التعليم على طريقة السؤال والجواب لهي:
• طريقةٌ نبويةٌ مفيدةٌ،
Teaching through the question-and-answer method is:
    • A beneficial Prophetic method.
وقد قال النبي ﷺ لمعاذ رضي الله عنه: «أتدري ما حق الله على العباد؟ وما حق العباد على الله؟»
The Prophet, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, said to Muʿāth (may Allāh be pleased with him): "Do you know what is the right of Allāh over His slaves? And what is the right of the slaves over Allāh?"
وقال ﷺ في حديث آخر: «إن من الشجر شجرة مثلها مثل المسلم لا يسقط ورقها أخبروني ما هي».
In another Hadith, he, ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam, said: "Indeed, among the trees there is a tree whose likeness is that of a Muslim; its leaves do not fall. Tell me, which one is it?"
وهذه الطريقة:
• أقرب إلى الفهم والتفهيم.
• وأوضح في التعلم والتعليم.
This method:
    • Is closer to [achieving] understanding and comprehension.
    • Is clearer for learning and teaching.
ومن هنا؛ فهذه مجموعة أسئلة يزيد عددها على الألف سؤال، كتبتها بطريقة مختصرة:
Hence, this is a collection of questions numbering more than a thousand, which I have written in a concise manner.
احتوت على أهم المهمات من أمور الدين، وأصول الإيمان، ومبادئ الفقه، والآداب، والمعاملات، والسيرة، وغيرها. تدعوا الحاجة والضرورة إلى معرفتها.
It contains the most important matters of religion: the foundations of faith (īmān), principles of jurisprudence (Fiqh), etiquette (Adab), transactions (Muʿāmalāt), biography (Sīrah), and others—matters for which there is a pressing need and necessity to know.
خصصتها للصغار ولا يستغني عنها الكبار.
I have designated it for the young, though adults cannot do without it either.
وقد تحريت جهدي أن تكون جميع الأسئلة مبنيةً على أدلة صحيحة من الكتاب والسنة.
I have strived to ensure all questions are based on authentic evidence from the Book and the Sunnah.
لكني لم أذكر الأدلة:
However, I did not mention the evidence [here]:
أولاً: لطلب الاختصار. ثانياً: لأن هذا سيكون -إن شاء الله- في كتاب آخر؛ يكون بمثابة الشرح والتوسع في هذه الأسئلة. ثالثاً: يكون هذا القدر من الجواب هو المطلوب من الصغير أن يحفظه، ويقوم المدرس بشرح الجواب، وذكر الدليل على ذلك.
    1.  For the sake of brevity.
    2.  Because this will be—if Allāh wills—in another book that will serve as an explanation and expansion of these questions.
    3.  So that this amount of the answer is what the child is required to memorize, while the teacher explains the answer and mentions the evidence for it.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary

نسأل الله أن ينفع بها أبناء المسلمين، وأن يجعلها من خير ما يدخر لنا عند رب العالمين. ونسأل الله أن يجزي خيراً من قام بمراجعتها، أو أعان على طبعها، والله الموفق والهادي إلى سواء السبيل.

messages.html:
Content

The app contains over 1,500 questions and answers, covering the pillars of faith, the names and attributes of Allāh, the prophets, the companions, the Qurʾān and its sciences, Islamic jurisprudence, biography of the Prophet ﷺ, etiquettes of daily life, and more. The Muntaqā edition (308 questions) includes a recorded audio recitation for every single question and answer.

---

Browse & Search

- Questions are organized into chapters and presented as interactive flip cards — tap a card to reveal the answer with a smooth 3D animation. 
- The full list loads progressively so even the largest book feels instant. 
- A search bar lets you find any question or answer in seconds, with fuzzy Arabic matching that handles spelling variations and strips diacritics automatically. 
- Search results highlight the matched text and auto-flip cards to the answer face when the match is found there. 
- You can filter by chapter at any time, both in the main view and inside search.

---

Favorites

- Any card can be starred and saved to a personal favorites list, which persists across sessions. 
- The favorites view gives you quick access to the questions you want to revisit most.

---

Quiz — Four Modes

The quiz section lets you test yourself on any chapter or the full book, with 5, 10, or 20 questions at a time. Four distinct modes keep practice engaging:

1. Multiple Choice — read the question and pick the correct answer from four options. 
2. Build the Answer — the answer is split into shuffled word tiles; tap them in the right order to reconstruct it. Placed tiles can be tapped again to return them to the pool. 
3. Fill in the Blank — the answer is shown with its most meaningful word hidden; choose the correct word from four options. 
4. Listen and Identify — the audio recording plays and you identify the correct answer from four choices, training your ear alongside your memory. 

- The app tracks your performance automatically. 
- Any question you get wrong more often than right gets flagged as a weak spot, and a dedicated *Weak Spots* section appears in the chapter selector so you can drill exactly what needs work.

---

Audio

- Every question in the Muntaqā edition has a native-quality audio recording. 
- Audio plays on both the front and back of flip cards, synced across both faces. 
- Audio also plays during the Listen quiz mode. 
- The app caches all 308 audio files in the background after the first visit, so they play offline without any delay.

---

Share

- Each card's back face has two sharing buttons: 
  - Copy — puts the question and answer text on your clipboard in one tap. 
  - Share as Image — generates a polished 1080×1080 card image with question, answer, chapter label, question number, gold ornaments, and app URL as a watermark; shares via the system share sheet on mobile or downloads on desktop. 
- The settings panel also has a share-link button that copies (or shares) a deep link to the current content and chapter.

---

Settings

- A settings panel (gear icon) gives three controls: 
  - Font size: small, medium, large 
  - High contrast mode for better readability in bright light 
  - Share-link button 
- Font size and contrast preference are saved and restored automatically on every visit.

---

Offline & Installable

- Full PWA: works entirely offline after the first visit.
- Installable to home screen on any device (iPhone, Android, desktop) and opens like a native app. 
- App shell updates silently in the background; users always get the latest version on next normal refresh. 
- No accounts. No ads. No tracking. Completely free.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
I'd really love if we stopped decorating people with labels, especially the living.
No matter how "big" someone seems.

Just call them shaykh and move on.

Saves you from exaggeration and from saying things that aren't true.

Some don't even deserve the title shaykh, yet it's been used so much it barely means anything now.

Dr. Fayṣal al-Wādiʿī still treats the word with weight and refuses to adopt it. More people like that would be nice. May Allāh bless him.

When al-Albānī lowered himself and al-Wādiʿī said, "we're basically nothing at this point", what does that say about the rest of us?

Yes, that was humility. But also honesty. They knew the level of the scholars before them and knew they were nowhere near them.

Strange thing: the lower the level gets, the bigger the labels become.

عجيب.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Lesson 2

1. What have the scholars said in explaining the greatness and significance of the long hadeeth of Jibreel?
2. Who is the scholar that said this hadeeth is the foundation of Islaam?
3. Who was the one who named this hadeeth “Umm as-Sunnah” (the Mother of the Sunnah)?
4. Who gave the best explanation of this hadeeth?
5. There are narrations other than the one in Saheeh Muslim that contain additional wording with beneficial points. Mention some of them, such as the Prophet, salla-llaahu 'alayahi wa sallam, being visible and prominent to the people, and that Jibreel, peace be upon him, greeted him and the Prophet, salla-llaahu 'alayahi wa sallam, returned the greeting.
6. How did ‘Umar, may Allaah be pleased with him, know that this man was not known to any of the Companions?
7. What benefit do we derive from his saying “You have spoken the truth” after asking the Prophet, salla-llaahu 'alayahi wa sallam, and receiving his answer?

https://arm-alqaddari.codeberg.page/compendiumCorrectCreed/lesson2/

messages.html:
تعبيرك عن رأيك في شخص ما، ليس نصيحة، النصيحة أن تبين الخطأ ثم كيفية تصويبه.

فإن أبديت رأيك ثم طلب منك بيان وجه ذلك فرفضت، فقد فعلت منكرا وأسأت لأخيك المسلم.

مثال:
زيد: فيك غلو يا أخي.
عمرو: كيف؟ بين لي هذا الغلو.
زيد: لا أريد النقاش، فقط اقبل النصيحة.

هنا، زيد طعن في عمرو، فقط. لم ينصحه. وفعله هذا من جنس السب والشتم. ولك أن تتخيل شعور عمرو، فهو الآن متهم بالغلو ولا يدري ما هذا الغلو.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Expressing your opinion about someone is not advice. Advice is to clarify the mistake and then explain how to correct it.

If you state your opinion and are then asked to explain it but refuse, you have committed a wrong and treated your Muslim brother badly.

Example:
Zayd: "You have extremism (ghulūww), my brother".
ʿAmr: "How? Explain this extremism to me".
Zayd: "I don’t want to discuss it. Just accept the advice".

Here, Zayd has merely attacked ʿAmr; he did not advise him. What he did is akin to insult and abuse. You can imagine how ʿAmr feels—he is now accused of extremism without even knowing what that extremism is.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Don't care for anyone who isn't willing to give and take. They're trying to control you, whether they realize that or not. You're not responsible for other people's subconscious.

A decent human being, who's humble and reasonable, has no problem discussing their positions or themselves.

Withholding while projecting is a sign of malicious intent, even if unintentional.

Falsehood and injustice are fed by veiling the truth or blocking paths to it.

One reason I love al-Albānī is the sheer amount of openness he had, even with deviants. He had no issue whatsoever to expose his mind to the other party.

"Here it is, I have nothing to hide, let's trade".

No one was able to beat him in a debate. Many were scared of debating him in the first place, even big scholars.

That's strength, not hiding away and trying to force your opinion on others.

A narrow mind goes not so far, and will disable any other mind that walks along with it.

messages.html:
Informing the People of ʾĪmān of the Detailed Ruling Regarding Sadness Over the Departure of Ramaḍān 🌙

The time of departure has drawn near, and just as we used to see messages of joy and longing, we now see messages of sadness and departure.

People have differed regarding the ruling on feeling sad over its departure. Some said it is not allowed, others said feeling sadness at its departure is like joy at its arrival.

The detailed answer is as follows:

Firstly: The original ruling is to show joy, due to the statement of the Prophet ﷺ

«There are two joys for the fasting person: the joy when he breaks his fast, and the joy of when he meets his Lord.»

Joy at breaking the fast is of two types.

1️⃣ Joy at the time of ifṭār at the end of the daily fast, and this is a recurring joy throughout the month.
2️⃣ Joy at the time of ʿĪd al-Fiṭr at the end of the monthly fast, and this is the final joy attached to breaking the fast. This is what is intended by the ḥadīth, and its meaning also includes the first [type].

Know that people, in their joy, are two types:
🔴 The first type:
A joy that entails hatred of fasting and happiness at being relieved from it. This is nonexistent except with hypocrites.
🟢 The second type:
A joy that does not mean relief from something hated, but rather a transition from one joy to another.

Accordingly, there are two joys:
● The joy of worship.
● The joy of completing worship.
All of this is permissible and legislated without doubt, and it is what is intended in the ḥadīth.

What remains is the summary of this situation: Is it correct to feel sadness over the departure of Ramaḍān?

The answer is from two angles.

The First Angle:
The original ruling is to show joy, based on two evidences:

1️⃣ The statement of Allāh:

"(He wants that you) must complete the same number (of days), and that you must magnify Allāh [i.e. to say Takbīr] for having guided you so that you may be grateful to Him."

This indicates joy from two aspects:
🌴 First: Takbīr
The takbīr at the end of fasting contradicts the display of sadness; rather, it is a symbol of joy, celebration, and gladness.
🌴 Second: Gratitude
Gratitude is not for a calamity, but for a blessing — and a blessing necessitates joy, not sadness.

2️⃣ Mentioned in the ḥadīth:

«There are two joys for the fasting person: the joy when he breaks his fast, and the joy of when he meets his Lord.»

Just as you do not feel sadness at meeting your Lord, likewise you should not feel sadness at breaking your fast as the two joys are paired together.

The Second Angle:
Sadness is an incidental matter that opposes the foundation, and it has two cases.

🚫 First case: That a person feels sad wishing Ramaḍān were longer, believing that this would be better. This sadness is invalid and a misguidance, because it opposes what Allāh has legislated, implying that something else is better than what Allāh decreed, and we seek refuge in Allāh.

✅️ Second case: That a person feels sad due to missing out on good because of his own shortcomings, negligence, or preoccupation. This is permissible, even if it comes late, as it is a form of regret over missing righteous deeds.

However, its permissibility is conditional upon not publicizing or displaying this sadness, because the Sharīʿah commands takbīr and joy. Thus, this is a private state that remains with the individual and should not extend to others.

*It was not from the way of the Salaf to display sadness during the days of ʿĪd at all; rather this contradicts their guidance.*

Written by: Abū al-ʿAbbās Anwar ibn Maḥmūd ar-Rifāʿī 1441 H
Tr: Umm Tamīm aṣ-Ṣūmāliyyah

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
الثاني: الشكر: فالشكر لا يكون على مصيبة بل يكون على نعمة، والنعمة تقتضي الفرح لا الحزن.
Second: Gratitude (shukr). Gratitude is not for a calamity; rather it is for a blessing—and a blessing calls for joy, not sorrow.



قلت: أما هذا فغلط، لأن شكر الله على المصائب من أعظم درجات الإيمان، إلا إن قال مصائب الدين، ولكن قوله هنا مطلق.
I said: This is incorrect. Thanking Allāh for calamities is among the greatest ranks of faith, unless one means calamities in religion. But his statement here is general.
وارتأيت نقل بيان تفصيل ذلك من كلام ابن عثيمين، رحمه الله:
I chose to transmit a clarification of this in detail from the words of Ibn ʿUthaymeen, رحمه الله:

وقد مر علينا أن مقامات الإنسان عند المصيبة أربعة، أربع مقامات.
It has already been mentioned that a person's states during a calamity are four—four ranks.
يبينها لنا شيبة؟
[Should] Shaybah reminds us of of them?
الطالب: التسخط ثم الصبر ثم الرضا ثم الشكر.
The student [Shaybah]: Discontent (tasakhkhuṭ), then patience (ṣabr), then contentment (riḍā), then gratitude (shukr).
الشيخ: نعم، أربع مقامات: التسخط، ثم الصبر، ثم الرضا، ثم الشكر.
The Shaykh: Yes—four ranks: discontent, then patience, then contentment, then gratitude.
التسخط محرم، ولهذا تبرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ممن تسخط.
Discontent is forbidden (ḥarām). That is why the Prophet ﷺ dissociated himself from the one who shows discontent.
قال: «ليس منا من ضرب الخدود وشق الجيوب ودعا بدعوى الجاهلية».
He said: "Not from us is the one who strikes the cheeks, tears the garments, and calls with the calls of Jāhiliyyah".
الصبر واجب، لأن الله تعالى أمر به في آيات كثيرة، والأصل في الأمر الوجوب.
Patience is obligatory (wājib), because Allāh commanded it in many āyāt—and the principle of a command is what? Obligation.
ولأنه لا معنى لعدم التسخط إلا الصبر.
Also, there is no real alternative to discontent except patience.
أما الرضا فإن في وجوبه لأهل العلم قولان، والصواب أنه سنة وليس بواجب.
As for contentment (riḍā), the scholars have two opinions regarding its obligation. The correct view is that it is encouraged (sunnah), not obligatory.
وأما الشكر فإنه مستحب بالاتفاق، وهو أعلى من الرضا.
As for gratitude (shukr), it is encouraged by consensus, and it is higher than contentment.

تفسير سورة البقرة، تفسير قوله تعالى: «وبشر الصابرين»، وذكر أحوال الناس في المصائب وهي أربعة: التسخط ثم الصبر ثم الرضا ثم الشكر، والفرق بين الرضا والصبر.

From the tafsīr of sūrat al-Baqarah, on the saying of Allāh: "And give glad tidings to the patient", and the mention of people's states in calamities—they are four: discontent, then patience, then contentment, then gratitude—and the difference between contentment and patience.

messages.html:
The Ruling on Giving Children Money on the Day of 'Eid

Question:
We have young children, and we are accustomed in our countries to give them—on the day of 'Eid, whether it is al-Fitr or al-Adha—what is called the "Eidiya." It consists of small amounts of money to bring joy to their hearts. Is this Eidiya an innovation (Bid’ah) or is there nothing wrong with it?

Answer:
There is no harm in that; rather, it is from the good customs and the bringing of happiness to a Muslim, whether old or young, which is a matter encouraged by the purified Legislation (Sharee’ah).

Shaykh ‘Abd al-’Azeez ibn ‘Abd Allaah ibn Baaz, Shaykh ‘Abd al-’Azeez Aal al-Shaykh, Shaykh Saalih al-Fawzaan, Shaykh Bakrin Abu Zayd.

Fatawa of the Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Ifta': (26/247)

Abu Juwayriyah

The Prevalence of Ignorance

Shaykh Ḥammād Al-Anṣārī (may Allāh have mercy on him) said:

“When I arrived at a place near Makkah, I met some Bedouins and asked their leader: ‘What are the pillars of Islam?’

He replied, ‘Ash-Shāfi‘ī, Abū Ḥanīfah, Mālik — and I forgot the fourth one!’

So I said to those around him, ‘Remind him — mention the fourth.’

They said, ‘We have forgotten.’

I then said to them, ‘Aḥmad (ibn Ḥanbal).’

They all exclaimed together, ‘Yes, that’s the one!’”

He added:

“This happened when we went out for da‘wah in the year 1375 AH.”

[Collected in his biography]

Source: https://t.me/madrasatuna/5339

التفريغ:

السائل: الحديث مع معاليكم لا يُمل، لكن لعلنا نختم بهذا السؤال، بعد إذن معاليكم، وهو سؤال يتكرر ودائم، عن مكتبتكم الكبرى، هل يمكن الحديث عن أهم مكوناتها أو نوادرها؟ ورأي معاليكم في اقتناء النوادر من الطبعات غالية الأثمان.

الشيخ: ما تسمعه بالعين خير من أن تراه.
الناس يذكرونها وهي ليست بحقيقية.
عندي [و]الحمد لله اقتناء، لكن ليس بمثل ما يصفونه، [هذا] الوصف الضخم. عندي اقتناء. وأحب الكتب القديمة، بشروط، وليس كل شيء.
والكتب من ملذات الحياة. لأن مجالسة الكتاب أحسن من مجالسة أي شيء في الدنيا.
وأنا ليس عندي أصدقاء ولا عندي مزرعة ولا عندي رحلات.
في الغالب، متعتي في هذا، أدور حول هذا.

أستغفر الله وأتوب اليه. سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك.



أتذكر هذه من فينة لأخرى.
تشبه ما قاله ابن المبارك لمن دعوه لمجالستهم.

messages.html:
Interviewer:
Speaking with Your excellency never becomes tiresome, but perhaps we will conclude with this question, if you permit. It is a question that is often repeated, about your great library. Could you speak about its most important components or its rare items? And what is your excellency's opinion regarding acquiring rare editions that are very expensive?

Ash-shaykh Ṣāliḥ Āl ash-Sheikh:
What you hear about it with the ear is better than seeing it with the eye.

People speak about it, but it is not really as they describe.

I do have acquisitions, al-ḥamdu liLlāh, but not as they portray it with that exaggerated description. I do have acquisitions.

I like old books—under certain conditions, not just anything.

Books are among the pleasures of life. Because keeping company with a book is better than keeping company with anything in the world.

I have no friends, no farm, and no trips.
Most of the time, my enjoyment is in this—I revolve around this.

I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him.

Subḥānaka Allāhumma wa bi-ḥamdik.

I remember this from time to time.

It resembles what Ibn al-Mubārak said when they invited him to sit with them.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Do I actually understand what I'm saying?

Q: Why do some people speak confidently about topics in general terms but struggle when asked for specifics?

A: Often because they're operating on impressions rather than structured understanding. A broad summary in their mind is enough for general conversation, but specifics require an internal model that may not exist.

Q: Why do people suddenly go blank when you ask them to explain details?

A: Psychologists call this the Illusion of Explanatory Depth — people think they understand something until they're asked to explain how it actually works.

Q: Why can someone know all the right words about a topic but still not really understand it?

A: Because vocabulary is not the same as structure. Someone may know the terms surrounding a subject but lack the internal connections that make those terms meaningful.

Q: Why do many conversations stay at a surface level?

A: Because most everyday conversation is social rather than analytical. The goal is participation and signaling, not precision.

Q: Why do specific questions make people uncomfortable?

A: Specific questions increase cognitive load — they force someone to construct a working explanation in real time. If the model isn't there, the mind stalls.

Q: Why do people sometimes become evasive instead of saying "I don't know"?

A: Because admitting ignorance can feel like a loss of status. Evasion protects face more easily than openly conceding uncertainty.

Q: What's a simple way to describe this pattern?

A: Talking at a general level is easy. Explaining how something actually works is hard, and that gap exposes whether real understanding is there or not.

Q: How can I recognize when someone is talking big but doesn't actually understand the topic?

A: Watch for these signs:

- They stay at generalities and avoid specifics.
- They use lots of words but don't connect ideas logically.
- When pressed, they become evasive, vague, or silent.
- They rely on buzzwords or repetition instead of examples or reasoning.

Spotting this helps you avoid wasting time on shallow talk and focus on meaningful discussion (good luck finding that) — or guide the conversation toward clarity if you want (good luck with that).

Q: How can understanding this pattern benefit me in daily life?

A: Use it on yourself first.

When you think you understand something, try to explain it clearly and specifically. If you can't, that's a sign your understanding is still incomplete.

This habit builds honesty with yourself, protects you from speaking without knowledge, and pushes you to seek clarity before forming strong opinions.

In religious matters especially, it helps practice humility, careful speech, and a deeper pursuit of knowledge — qualities essential for a Muslim who wants to act upon knowledge rather than impressions.
