messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
The Second Mountain of Daʿwah
---

Daʿwah is not merely the delivery of correct information.
It is an interaction with hearts.

That statement is gold. اللهم بارك.

It reflects a reality that many callers to Islām eventually discover through experience.

At first, one assumes that the main problem is a lack of correct knowledge. If people only received the authentic evidence clearly and properly explained, surely the matter would become straightforward.

In many cases, this assumption is partly correct.

But after climbing that first mountain—the mountain of clarifying the truth—another mountain suddenly appears.

The second mountain is the human heart.

People are rarely willing to abandon their current reality overnight. Their habits, attachments, social pressures, fears, and desires all stand in the way. Not every person possesses the readiness of someone like Abū Bakr رضي الله عنه, who accepted the truth immediately once it became clear.

For most people, the struggle is not only intellectual. It is emotional, social, and psychological.

And this is where the second mountain begins.

The Prophetic Model of Patience
---

The Prophets endured extraordinary levels of ignorance and resistance over long periods of time.

They did not immediately declare:

"You have now heard the truth in its purest form. You have no excuse. I will supplicate against you".

They only reached that stage after it became clear that the issue was no longer difficulty accepting the truth, but rather deliberate rejection and obstinate disbelief.

Until that point, patience remained the dominant method.

This is a crucial distinction.

Guidance is not only about presenting the truth; it is about allowing the truth time to settle within hearts.

The Methodology of the Scholars
---

This principle can also be seen in the conduct of the great scholars.

A clear example is al-Albānī رحمه الله, who debated major deviants across decades. He engaged them calmly, repeatedly, and patiently, while still warning against their errors.

That balance is important.

Patience and gentleness did not mean abandoning clarification of falsehood. At the same time, refutation did not turn into uncontrolled hostility.

Unfortunately, some people today fall into one of two extremes:

* Either they abandon warning against deviation in the name of "gentleness".
* Or they abandon wisdom and patience in the name of "defending the truth".

The correct methodology lies between these two extremes.

What About the Common People?
---

If patience was required with kuffār and even with known deviants, then what about ordinary Muslims?

Common people often carry confusion, cultural habits, incomplete knowledge, and emotional attachments that have developed over decades.

Changing these things rarely happens quickly.

Calling people to the truth is therefore not a short project.

It is not even a lifetime project.

In reality, it is a continuous effort across generations, lasting until Allāh takes the last believer from the earth.

A Test for the Caller
---

Daʿwah is not only a test for the people being called.

It is equally a test for the one calling.

During times of trials—when the correct understanding of Islām is attacked, distorted, and marginalized—the bond between the caller and the people becomes extremely delicate.

If that cord is pulled too harshly, it may snap.

And if it snaps, the opportunity for guidance disappears.

Imagine asking people to stand with you while the entire environment around them portrays your position as extreme, strange, or dangerous. Even when the truth is clear, people still need help overcoming the psychological weight of that decision.

This is where gentleness becomes one of the essential ingredients of the cure.

But gentleness alone is not enough.

The other ingredient is deep and correct knowledge.

The Role of the Imāms
---

The history of Islām shows that true imāms are rare.

Across millions of Muslims in every era, only a small number rise to the level of guiding entire communities with wisdom, balance, and clarity.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Each era presents unique challenges.

Each era produces its own trials.

The great imāms were those who could understand their time, address its specific problems, and apply the principles of Islām with precision while remaining firmly rooted in the methodology of the Salaf.

This responsibility is immense.

And it is something that must not be treated lightly.

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

3rd of Shawwāl, 1447 AH

messages.html:
So, What Enjoyment Can be Similar To It?

عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: «الدُّنْيَا مَتَاعٌ، وَخَيْرُ مَتَاعِ الدُّنْيَا الْمَرْأَةُ الصَّالِحَةُ»

Abdullah bin ‘Amrin - may Allaah be pleased with them both - reported that the Messenger of Allaah ﷺ said: "The world is enjoyment, and the best enjoyment of the world is the righteous woman."

Sahih Muslim (1467)

Commentary from the Scholar
Al-’Allaamah Mudhhir ad-Deen az-Zaydaani (d. 727 AH, may Allaah have mercy upon him):

The best thing from which a man derives benefit is the righteous woman. For indeed, he finds pleasure in her, and she is a source of tranquility and companionship for him. She protects his eyes and his private parts from the forbidden (Haram), and she assists him in his religion by preventing him from falling short in acts of obedience. Through her, he attains children who obey Allaah, thereby increasing the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. So, what enjoyment among the enjoyments of this world could have a benefit like the benefit of a righteous woman?

Al-Mafateeh fi Sharh al-Masabeeh (4/9)

Translated by
Ummu Hayaa's Majlis

messages.html:
You'd realize much stronger how rare and good a Salafi woman is if you see how other women are, especially disbelievers.

A huge source of agony and distress are women who know not their Rabb.

So, yā akhi, we should be much more careful with such gems. Aye?!

The amount of courage they have, to go against the current trends and society, is fascinating to say the least. اللهم بارك.

I've seen women have mini panic attacks if they're told to just wear a head cover.

Not to mention the tranquility they radiate, even if they have their own struggles (who doesn't). They're full of admonition and advices from scholars about being patient and seeking reward for that. They believe in that!

Now, the same applies to you akhi, you're also a rare gem. We should also be careful with you and appreciate you for the decisions you made. Don't worry, Allāh decreed this for you, you think He'd abandon you midway? That'd be your fault, you weren't sincere.

—A Salafi man who once wasn't Salafi

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Step By Step, And You'll Grow So Big

Remember, do not think about tasks whole—your brain will choke.

"You mad?!", said the brain.
"Release depression and failure hormones!!!", the brain as well.

Divide a single task into sub-tasks.

فرق، تسود
Farriq, tasood.
Divide them, and you'll conquer them.

"Ohh....that's more like it!", says the brain.
"Ok ok ok, kill the depression switch, this human is back into his mind, being reasonable and all", the brain as well.

Humans love jumping to conclusions, it's easier, requires less effort, less scary.

1+1=11

Why do maths if you can stick them together?

That's what happens when you don't think through decisions and conclusions.

One decision like that after another, they snowball, and now you think you're a failure who's behind everyone and can't seem to be motivated to do anything. It always ends up locked...

Slow down, step by step, and you'll get there.

In Algeria, we tell toddlers who try to walk:
"داداش، تكبر قداش"
"Dāddāsh, tekber qaddāsh"
It's baby talk, not really Arabic.
Meaning, step by step, and you'll grow so big.

Imagine that toddler thinking about racing in the Olympics or whatever.

I can imagine the life draining out of their eyes. Such a huge gap.

But even the fastest runner was a toddler once.

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
How do you recommend people to improve when it comes to programming?

Simple, actually. Just make projects once you know the basics.

Go gradual, tiny, small, medium, then big.

Identify your goal. Programming is just a tool. If you have no goal, it's useless and you'll feel lost because you have no destination.

Start a mini project, something that interests you personally. You'll encounter problems. You'll learn by solving them. That's it.

You'll have the drive to reach your destiny, and those problems will be hurdles you need to get over. Solving those problems is what software development is about.

Practice! Practice! Practice!

Everyday if you can. A short session everyday goes a long way.

That's enough, I believe. Further questions are welcome.

messages.forwardedFrom: Markaz Abu Hurayrah | مركز أبي هريرة
messages.html:
Sisterly Benefits #2 — A Powerful Parable Describing True Sisterhood (& Brotherhood) 🎀

The Messenger of Allāh ﷺ said:

“مَثَلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي تَوَادِّهِمْ وَتَرَاحُمِهِمْ وَتَعَاطُفِهِمْ، مَثَلُ الْجَسَدِ، إِذَا اشْتَكَى مِنْهُ عُضْوٌ، تَدَاعَى لَهُ سَائِرُ الْجَسَدِ بِالسَّهَرِ وَالْحُمَّى”

“The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, their mutual mercy, and their mutual compassion is like a single body: when one limb complains, the rest of the body responds to it with sleeplessness and fever.”

[Sahīḥ Muslim (2586), also in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī (6011) with a slightly different wording]

——

Some Benefits Derived From The Ḥadīth

1] The Specific Arabic Wording Indicates Necessary Mutual Qualities Amongst The Believers

The words تَوَادّ, تَرَاحُم, and تَعَاطُف are verbal nouns built on reciprocal feelings and actions. They indicate love, mercy, and compassion that must be exchanged between believers, not one-sided. Translating them as “mutual love, mutual mercy, and mutual compassion” preserves this meaning, showing that the relationship between believers in acts of goodness must consistently involve both giving and receiving.

2] Each Word Reflects a Different Layer of Sisterhood/Brotherhood

The Prophet ﷺ mentioned three distinct qualities, not repeating one term:
• Loving affection between believers — تَوَادّ
• Mutually showing mercy — تَرَاحُم
• Actively sympathising with and supporting one another — تَعَاطُف

Together, these describe a relationship between believers consisting of continuous love in the heart, mercy in behaviour, and support in action. The absence of any of these shows a deficiency in the true actualisation of Īmān (belief).

3] “Complains” and “Responds”: The Collective Interaction

The verb اشْتَكَى literally means “to complain of pain.” Translating it as “aches” weakens the imagery. The wording emphases a limb outwardly expressing distress/discomfort, prompting the rest of the body to react accordingly.

The verb تَدَاعَى describes parts calling and responding to one another. The body cannot remain passive; it mobilises in response. Similarly, a believer cannot ignore the discomforts and hardships of fellow Muslims—action must follow awareness.

4] The Reaction Described Is Involuntary

Sleeplessness (السَّهَر) and fever (الْحُمَّى) are natural instinctive bodily responses. The parable therefore illustrates that a believer’s concern for other believers must also be instinctive. Hearing a fellow Muslim’s pain must naturally move the heart and provoke action.

——

Conclusion

The Prophet ﷺ did not describe believers as people who occasionally care for one another. He described them as a single body that cannot ignore the pain of any part.

If the suffering of a Muslim does not disturb our hearts, occupy our thoughts, and move us to act, then we must question whether this description truly applies to us.

A body that feels nothing and takes no action when a limb is in pain is unhealthy—it is numb or lifeless. Likewise, a believer who does not act to support a fellow believer has failed in their duty.

This is the true likeness of a believer: the heart aches for one another, and the limbs demonstrate that care through action.

As the Arabic proverb goes:

وكلٌّ يَدَّعِي وَصْلًا بِلَيْلَى * وَلَيْلَى لا تُقِرُّ لهم بِذَاكَا

Everyone claims affiliation to Laylā * but Laylā does not affirm it for them.

Do not be a false claimant of Īmān. Embody the obligations toward your fellow believers—love, mercy, and support must be lived, not just spoken.

كتبه أبو رفق آدم
٥ شوال ١٤٤٧ هـ
Source: https://t.me/markazabuhurayrah

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Things Are Not Always What They Seem

At first glance, you might say: “This is potatoes and eggs.” But in reality, it’s completely different.

What looks like potatoes is actually apples. The “egg yolk” isn’t yolk—it’s a peach. And the “egg white” isn’t egg—it’s yogurt.

Be careful. Don’t believe every piece of news or repeat things you’re not sure about. Not everything you see should be believed, and not everything you hear is true. Don’t judge others based only on appearances. Take your time and don’t rush. Avoid سوء الظن (thinking badly of others) and oppression.

Listen directly from me, not about me. Stay away from gossipers, backbiters, and those who bring others down—and everything will be fine.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
You can learn with time and practice to be cautious and aware of what you believe and accept.

On the other hand, please don't share everything you see, and consider whether what you shared personally resonates with you.

Why? Because you have a much better chance of understanding it and its consequences than something you superficially agree with.

Doesn't mean what you share must be scarce. You can still produce in high volumes if you could. People are different.

One last point: It's good to conform to established systems, because that brings more order and restraint. But please be careful of falling in blind following. Even salafis suffer from that. Just a different flavor.

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

messages.html:
hhhhh

الله المستعان.

شر البلية ما يضحك.

When we warn against social media like Facebook and the rest of the circus, we're called extremists, even by some Salafis.

"Why are you running away? Why are you letting the kuffār have all the space?"

Let them have it. Just like I'm willing to let them have bars and casinos.

Knowledge has dignity. If it weren't for the strong presence of Salafis and the ability to control content on Telegram, I wouldn't even entertain the thought of being here, I even left once, but changed my mind after reconsidering the pros and cons.

I made an analogy in my book al-Buzoogh:
"Leaving an asthma patient in a highly polluted area, then throwing medicine at them from afar".

Teach people the harms of these platforms, and guide them to better ones, then do daʿwah. Allāh yahdīk.

It's also the fault of tech-savy brothers, they don't spread much awareness about the possible alternatives.

والله المستعان.
The point is, no one reasonable and knowledgeable enough would use that stuff. You should feel chest tightness by merely entering them.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Words vs. Action

We all love to talk about love. Mercy. Care. Brotherhood. Sisterhood. Doing good. Helping others.

Because, it sounds nice, and it feels good. Because, it is safe.

Here comes the:
However,
when someone actually creates something. A project. A resource. Something that could make a difference, something that could use a bit of attention, a tiny response. The room suddenly gets quiet.

*crickets sounds*

Polite words, maybe.
Engagement? Rare.
Feedback? Even rarer.

That makes one ask if the effort even landed.
Waiting for a reaction that never comes.

And it's not personal. Not really. It's just human.

Talking is cheap. Action costs.

Another plot twist!

We'll happily spend hours discussing books, analyzing states, chasing trends. Because that's comfortable, visible, easy.

But giving five minutes to someone else's work? That's the expensive version of caring. "It's optional".

We all do it sometimes. Admit it. Sometimes we're the quiet ones. Sometimes we're the distracted ones. Tired.

I'm tired, he's tired, she's tired, everyone's tired.

We created a gap, a gap between words and action, which is where sincerity shows.

It's also where effort quietly dies, unnoticed, unremarked, unappreciated—not because it wasn't valuable, but because attention is scarce. "We're all tired".

It doesn't have to be complicated. If someone produces something—even small, even imperfect—respond. Share (ok you don't have to share). Encourage (!!).

Give a few minutes.

Not as a favor. Not for praise. Just as humans. That's all it takes.

Words are easy. Action proves them.

The tiny, quiet proof, is what makes love, care, and support real.

Everything else? Noise.

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

messages.html:
To the sister who feels strange in her jilbāb

Know, my beloved sister in īmān, that you will always feel like a gharībah (stranger).

Know that by following the commandments of Allāh and His Messenger ﷺ, you will be faced with insults and mockery.

Know that many will look at your garments with hatred in their hearts.

Know that the majority will never be pleased with you.

But know that the glad tidings are for the ghurabāʾ.

لَتُبْلَوْنَ فِي أَمْوَلِكُمْ وَأَنفُسِكُمْ وَلَتَسْمَعُنَّ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتُبَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُواْ أَذَى كَثِيرًا وَإِن تَصْبِرُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ الْأَمُورِ

You shall certainly be tried and tested in your wealth and properties and in your personal selves, and you shall certainly hear much that will grieve you from those who received the Scripture before you (Jews and Christians) and from those who ascribe partners to Allāh; but if you persevere patiently, and become Al-Muttaqūn (the pious) then verily, that will be a determining factor in all affairs (and that is from the great matters which you must hold
on with all your efforts).

– [Sūrah Āli ʿImrān: 186]

We are here to be tested. We are here to be tried. Bear these tests with patience as the righteous before us did.

Let them speak.
Let them mock.
Let them ridicule.

Your value is not in their approval. Your worth is not measured by the amount of praise you receive, how many compliments you get, or how much the world approves of you.

Your value is with Allāh and obeying Him ﷻ.

You are wearing the garments of the righteous — the clothing of dignity — the attire of those who chase the ākhirah.

So let not your heart long for the praise of those who chase the adornments of this dunyā.

Dress for His pleasure, seek His approval.
The only approval you need is His.

For you will find your reward with Allāh, and He is ash-Shakūr (the Most Appreciative).

Jannah is for the people who are strange. Those who enjoin others in righteousness and piety. Those who correct what the people have corrupted of the Sunnah. Those who remain steadfast on this path despite the hardship they face.

Hold firmly to your dīn dear sisters. Hold firmly to the Sunnah. Hold firmly to the way of our salaf (pious predecessors).

For indeed, blessed are the strangers.

The Prophet ﷺ said:

"بَدَأَ الإِسْلاَمُ غَرِيبًا وَسَيَعُودُ كَمَا بَدَأَ غَرِيبًا فَطُوبَى لِلْغُرَبَاءِ‏"
“Islam began as something strange and it will return to being strange, so glad tidings to the strangers.”
[Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 145]



- أم مصعب الغانية الألمانية

messages.html:
Your value is not in their approval. Your worth is not measured by the amount of praise you receive, how many compliments you get, or how much the world approves of you.

Your value is with Allāh and obeying Him ﷻ.

Note that ash-Shayṭān always tries to dig at your tawḥīd, and that's a very common route he takes: playing with your ego and insecurities.

If you don't resist the urge to satisfy those desires, you'll only go further from what Allāh commands, because those don't satisfy your desires, in your skewed point of view.

Just like people who get used to eat junk food find it hard to enjoy healthy food. Try to convince a very unhealthy teenager to eat steamed veggies with a drizzle of olive oil, homemade cheese, and rock salt.

That's very appetising to a normal healthy human being. But that teenager? Too stuffed with chemicals to realize that, because he let himself indulge into the void of junk.

A healthy normal person enjoys decent and dignified clothing. That's sound fiṭrah. Remember that being clothed is a bliss in al-Jannah, explicitly mentioned in revelation.

والعياذ بالله من شرهم.

messages.html:
It's ok to use tools that help you polish your writing, as long as that doesn't cripple your reasoning and ability to produce.

Life is short, and you're here to prepare for reckoning. Use the easier route if it helps with that, and doesn't negatively affect you.

Not every tool is a strict necessity, just because it was used by our salaf, they were also just trying to adopt the best system based on what was available to them.

Read more about them, and you'll be surprised how they used to think regarding that. It's so refreshing.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
The Future Isn't AI vs Designers. It's Designers With AI

Designers keep hearing the same sentence lately:
"AI will replace you".

But that sentence misunderstands both design and AI.

AI is a tool.
A powerful one, yes. But still a tool.
It can generate images, layouts, color palettes, and variations in seconds.

What it cannot do is understand context, culture, nuance, or intent the way a human designer can. It doesn't know why something should feel subtle instead of dramatic, calm instead of loud, or restrained instead of flashy. It simply predicts patterns.

Anyone who has worked with AI for more than five minutes has seen this. The strange quirks. The overly dramatic compositions. The details that almost make sense but somehow miss the point.

That's where designers come in.
A good designer brings taste, judgment, restraint, and understanding. Those things do not come from data alone. They come from experience, observation, and thinking about people.

AI doesn't remove the need for those things. If anything, it increases it.

Without a designer guiding it, AI produces noise. With a designer guiding it, AI becomes incredibly powerful.

The designer is no longer just the person moving pixels. The designer becomes the one directing the system.

Instead of saying:
'AI stole my job'.

A smarter response is:
'I know how to control that AI and turn it into something useful'.

The people who thrive in the future will not be the ones who ignore AI or fear it. They will be the ones who learn how to guide it, refine it, and push it toward better outcomes.

Design has always been about solving problems.

AI simply gives designers a faster set of tools.

And a designer who knows how to think will always outperform a machine that can only predict.

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

messages.html:
🌱 Understanding the Nature of Children

When you understand the nature of children, many things that would normally cause frustration become easier to bear with patience and wisdom.

A young child — from birth to usually around four years old — naturally sees the world as revolving around them, everything belongs to them in their head. They may take things that don’t belong to them or refuse to share, not out of bad intention, rather it's their nature, they haven’t yet developed the concept of ownership or the awareness of others — they'll eventually grow out of it if you teach them well with gentleness.

So instead of reacting with anger, you respond by teaching them with patience and ḥilm (forbearance). They are not disobeying out of bad intention, but lack of understanding.

Similarly, younger children are naturally drawn to what they can see and experience more than what they are told.

If, for example, an eight year old child delays prayer or prefers playing games over ḥifẓ, it's not because they hate worship or reject obedience to Allāh, rather, it is because:

The ghayb (unseen) is still abstract to them, while the dunya is immediate and tangible. So they don't want to "miss out" on the fun while praying or memorising.

And this is something even adults struggle with, let alone children.

So tarbiyah here requires:

• Gradual nurturing of īmān
• Patience over years, not days
• Consistency without harshness

You plant the seed early, but you don’t expect the tree to grow overnight.

This also extends beyond children.

When you understand people's nature, you begin to deal with them with wisdom, not mere reactions.

• A man who understands emotional fluctuations may show more patience and sympathy instead of taking things personally.

• A woman who understands that anger is a human nature Allāh trialed men with especially may respond with more restraint instead of provocatively.

So you deal with people with their level of understanding — not your own.

With that said, this understanding is an excuse for others, but not a justification for ourselves.

You assume the best of your Muslim brothers and sisters, you excuse them, you show mercy.

But you also hold yourself accountable, you strive against the blameworthy traits you were tested with, you don’t hide behind “this is just my nature”.

- كتبته أم عبدالرحمن السودانية،
٦ شوال ١٤٧٧هـ

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Not Every Path to Rizq Runs Through a Company

Many people assume that earning a living must follow one path:

School → University → Job → Salary.

But this model is only one way people organize work. It is not the only way.

In many parts of the tech world, people build something different. Instead of creating companies, they create projects.

These projects are often open source. Developers from different places contribute, improve the work, and build around it.

The project grows over time, and eventually it can be monetized in different ways: services, premium features, support, sponsorships, or related tools.

The key difference is independence.
Instead of entering an existing system and becoming a small piece inside it, a person builds something that belongs to them.

It takes initiative and patience, because in the beginning there is no salary waiting at the end of the month. There is only tawakkul and effort.

But if the work is solid and beneficial, momentum begins to build.
People start using the project. Others contribute. Opportunities appear.

What began as a small effort slowly becomes a sustainable source of income.

This model already exists and is widely used. It's just that the majority are terrified of it.

It simply requires a different mindset.
It requires someone willing to think beyond the usual path and take responsibility for their own work.

For Muslims, this independence can also allow more freedom to dedicate time and effort to beneficial work and daʿwah, without being tied to structures that may restrict it.

In the end, every path to provision comes from the same place:

وما توفيقي إلا بالله

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
وَمِنْ طَرَائِفِ الْوَسْوَاسِ:
Among the oddities of obsessive reasoning

احْتِجَاجُ ابْنِ بُكَيْرٍ الْمَالِكِيِّ فِي أَنَّهَا لَيْلَةُ سَبْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ
is the argument of Ibn Bukayr al-Māliki that Laylat al-Qadr is the twenty-seventh night.

بِقَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى:
He based this on the statement of Allāh, Exalted is He:

{سَلامٌ هِيَ} [القدر: 5]
'Salāmun hiya' (Peace it is) [al-Qadr: 5].

قَالَ:
He said:

فَلَفْظَةُ " هِيَ "
the word 'hiya'

هِيَ السَّابِعَةُ وَعِشْرُونَ مِنْ السُّورَةِ.
is the twenty-seventh word of the sūrah.

قَالَ أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ:
Abū Muḥammad (Ibn Ḥazm) said:

حَقُّ مَنْ قَامَ هَذَا فِي دِمَاغِهِ
The one in whose mind such a notion arises

أَنْ يُعَانِيَ بِمَا يُعَانِي بِهِ سُكَّانُ الْمَارَسْتَانِ
deserves to be treated the way the residents of the māristān (insane asylum) are treated.

نَعُوذُ بِاَللَّهِ مِنْ الْبَلَاءِ،
We seek refuge in Allāh from affliction.

وَلَوْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ مِنْ هَذَا أَكْثَرُ مِنْ دَعْوَاهُ
And if he had nothing from this except his claim

أَنَّهُ وَقَفَ عَلَى مَا غَابَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ
that he has discovered something

عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ -
that remained hidden from the Muhammad ﷺ

وَلَمْ يَنْسَ مِنْ عِلْمِ الْغَيْبِ
and that he did not forget from the knowledge of the unwitnessed

مَا أَنْسَاهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ نَبِيَّهُ - عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ -،
what Allāh, Mighty and Majestic, caused His Prophet to forget

وَمَنْ بَلَغَ إلَى هَذَا الْحَدِّ
Whoever reaches such a level

فَجَزَاؤُهُ أَنْ يَخْذُلَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى
then his recompense is that Allāh abandons him

مِثْلَ هَذَا الْخِذْلَانِ الْعَاجِلِ
to such disgraceful abandonment in this world

ثُمَّ فِي الْآخِرَةِ أَشَدُّ تَنْكِيلًا.
and in the Hereafter the punishment will be even more severe.

[ابن حزم ,المحلى بالآثار ,4/459]

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Revisit

I loved Ibn Hazm long before I knew other scholars. I didn't even know who Al-Albany was.

Ibn Hazm taught me how to be free, how to think from the ground up, how to dissect concepts, how to destroy arguments.

How to rely on the salaf. How to take the Qur'aan and Sunnah as the absolute source of truth.

I like what they call "his rigidity", it's a unique and powerful way of thinking. Many who criticize him for it wouldn't stand a chance against him and would need to concede to his arguments. He's very persuasive, strong in debates.

One of my wishes is a debate between him and Ibn Taymiyyah...

He's human of course, made mistakes, but it's very obvious he sought the truth. We can never claim otherwise.

May Allāh have mercy on him, and grant him al-Firdaws al-A’lā.

messages.html:
السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته

Consider making books into simple PWAs using vanilla JS, HTML, and CSS.

It's a great way to trick people into reading books these days.

An app feels much interesting to them than a PDF or a printed book.

Especially if it looks nice and sleek.

Example:
https://t.me/abuSahlInventory/44

You can easily monetize such projects by making them freemium.

Make the free features enough to be considered a full app, and add luxury as paid options. Some people would buy them just to support such initiatives.

The door is wide open. Be one of the first to take advantage. You'd be hitting two birds with one stone.

There's too many books, you can't even scratch the tip of the iceberg.

Tip: leverage vibe-coding.

ان شاء الله.

messages.html:
السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته،

A small (?) update for this project.

I created a blog for the channel:
https://islaamchildrenbooks.blogspot.com/

The content is the same as here. Nothing new, nothing different.

Why?

Simply, because Telegram channels are not very discoverable. Parents searching on the web will almost never find a Telegram channel, but they can find a blog.

So the blog exists to make this content easier to discover for families who are searching online.

If you know parents looking for beneficial Islamic children's books, sharing the blog link might help them find it.

Also a small (?) reminder: blogs are still extremely useful. They are simple, searchable, and accessible to anyone on the web.

Sometimes the "old tools" are still the best ones.

You don't have to click all the buttons the software offers you, you know.

messages.html:
السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته،

حياكم الله.

I'd like your opinion on something regarding the channel.

What do you think about allowing reactions in channels?

Yes?
No?
Depends?

You can probably guess that I currently do not allow them. I don't see much benefit in them, and I worry that reactions can slowly influence what a person chooses to post. Even if someone believes they are unaffected, it is easy for reactions to start shaping content over time.

Because of that, I prefer removing them entirely so the poster remains as natural and unaffected as possible.

However, I still value outside perspectives. Fresh eyes often notice things one misses without discussion.

If you have thoughts on the matter, feel free to share them here:

https://forms.gle/aBrZ61L8uPhSQciu6

messages.html:
السائل : ورد أن الله سبحانه وتعالى يبعث على رأس كل قرن هجري مجددا لهذه الأمة فهل هذا صحيح أولا ؟ وإن كان صحيحا فما نوع التجديد الذي يتم على يد هذا المجدد ؟
الشيخ : الحديث صحيح، والتجديد أنواع هذا هو الصحيح في تفسير الحديث فالإسلام يحتاج إلى تجديد كلما مضى عليه برهة من الزمن طويل أو قصير.
وتجديد الإسلام يكون من نواحي متعددة أهمها تجديد مفاهيمه الصحيحة حيث ينحرف المسلمون مع الزمن عن فهم الإسلام كتابا وسنة فهما صحيحا فأعظم تجديد هو هذا المجدد الذي يأتي إلى المسلمين بالمفاهيم الصحيحة التي كان عليها سلفنا الصالح لنصوص الكتاب والسنة ومن هذا التجديد الأهم هو أن يصفي السنة مما دخل فيها مما ليس منها ثم هو يدعو المسلمين إلى الإعتماد على هذه السنة الصحيحة مع القرآن ومع ذاك البيان الصحيح لكل منهما الذي كان عليه سلفنا الصالح . هذا التجديد وهو أهم تجديد ولا تقوم قائمة المسلمين وقائمة الحركات الإسلامية والدعوات كلها الإسلامية والأحزاب الإسلامية كلها إلا إذا بنيت على هذا التجديد الأصيل .
تجديد السنة بتمييز ما ليس منها وطرحها جانبا وتجديد المفاهيم الصحيحة لنصوص الكتاب والسنة لدعوة المسلمين إلى المفاهيم التي كان عليها سلفنا الصالح لكن هذا في الواقع لا يكفي لا بد هناك من تجديد مثلا لعلوم أخرى يتطلب تطور الحياة العلمية والإجتماعية أن يتوجه بعض الناس إلى تجديدها ونضرب على ذلك مثلا علم اللغة فهذا العلم لا بد من التجديد فيه وتقريبه إلى الناس حتى العرب أنفسهم الذين ابتعدوا قليلا أو كثيرا عن لغتهم بسبب العجمة التي تسربت إليهم فلا بد إذا من تجديد العلم وكذلك يقال لا بد من تجديد النواحي التربوية والنفسية وتوجيه المسلمين إلى ما يوافق أيضا الكتاب والسنة من هذه النواحي كلها، ولا شك أن فردا بل جماعة لا تستطيع أن تقوم بكل هذه الجهود وهذه التجديدات ولذلك ذكر بعض العلماء كمثال لأنواع التجديد ذكر من المجددين صلاح الدين الأيوبي مع أن الرجل لم يكن مشهورا بالعلم ولكن لما جدد الحياة الإسلامية بأن حضهم على الجهاد وحملهم على مقاتلة الأعداء وإخراجهم من البلاد بعد أن احتلوها سنين طويلة فاعتبروه من جملة المجددين .
فإذا التجديد لا يحصر في ناحية دون أخرى فما دامت الحياة تتجدد فلا بد أيضا من العلوم من أن تتجدد وأن تنشأ هذه العلوم وفق الكتاب والسنة الصحيحة وعلى المفهوم الذي كان عليه سلفنا الصالح رضي الله عنهم .

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
A Renewer Of This Era Was Asked: What Types Of Renewal Are There?

السائل: ورد أن الله سبحانه وتعالى يبعث على رأس كل قرن هجري مجددًا لهذه الأمة فهل هذا صحيح أولًا؟

Questioner: There is a report that Allāh, Glorified and Exalted be He, raises up at the turn of every Hijrī century a renewer (mujaddid) for this Ummah — is this report, first of all, authentic?

وإن كان صحيحًا فما نوع التجديد الذي يتم على يد هذا المجدد؟

And if so, what is the nature of the renewal brought about by this renewer?

الشيخ: الحديث صحيح، والتجديد أنواع — هذا هو الصحيح في تفسير الحديث.

The Sheikh: The ḥadīth is authentic, and renewal is of various types — this is the sound interpretation of the ḥadīth.

فالإسلام يحتاج إلى تجديد كلما مضى عليه برهة من الزمن طويل أو قصير.

Islām stands in need of renewal whenever any stretch of time has passed over it, long or short.

وتجديد الإسلام يكون من نواحٍ متعددة أهمها تجديد مفاهيمه الصحيحة.

The renewal of Islām takes place on multiple fronts, the most important of which is renewing its correct understandings.

حيث ينحرف المسلمون مع الزمن عن فهم الإسلام كتابًا وسنةً فهمًا صحيحًا.

For with the passage of time, Muslims drift away from a sound grasp of Islām — its Book and its Sunnah alike.

فأعظم تجديد هو هذا المجدد الذي يأتي إلى المسلمين بالمفاهيم الصحيحة التي كان عليها سلفنا الصالح لنصوص الكتاب والسنة.

The greatest renewal, therefore, is that of the renewer who comes to the Muslims bearing the correct understandings that our Righteous Predecessors (Salaf aṣ-Ṣāliḥ) held regarding the texts of the Book and the Sunnah.

ومن هذا التجديد الأهم هو أن يصفّي السنة مما دخل فيها مما ليس منها.

Central to this most vital form of renewal is also that he cleanse the Sunnah of what has crept into it that does not belong to it.

ثم هو يدعو المسلمين إلى الاعتماد على هذه السنة الصحيحة مع القرآن ومع ذاك البيان الصحيح لكل منهما الذي كان عليه سلفنا الصالح.

Then he calls the Muslims to ground themselves in this authenticated Sunnah alongside the Qurʾān, together with the sound understanding of both that our Righteous Predecessors were upon.

هذا التجديد وهو أهم تجديد، ولا تقوم قائمة المسلمين وقائمة الحركات الإسلامية والدعوات الإسلامية كلها والأحزاب الإسلامية كلها إلا إذا بُنيت على هذا التجديد الأصيل.

This is the renewal, and it is the most important of all. Muslims cannot find their footing — nor can Islamic movements, Islamic daʿwah efforts, or Islamic parties — unless they are built upon this foundational renewal.

تجديد السنة بتمييز ما ليس منها وطرحها جانبًا، وتجديد المفاهيم الصحيحة لنصوص الكتاب والسنة لدعوة المسلمين إلى المفاهيم التي كان عليها سلفنا الصالح.

Renewing the Sunnah — by identifying what does not belong to it and setting it aside — and renewing the correct understandings of the texts of the Book and Sunnah in order to call Muslims to the understandings that our Righteous Predecessors held.

لكن هذا في الواقع لا يكفي.

This, however, is not sufficient in itself.

لا بد هناك من تجديد لعلوم أخرى يتطلب تطور الحياة العلمية والاجتماعية أن يتوجه بعض الناس إلى تجديدها.

There must also be renewal in other fields of knowledge that the advancement of scholarly and social life demands certain people dedicate themselves to.

ونضرب على ذلك مثلًا علم اللغة.

Take, for example, the science of the Arabic language.

فهذا العلم لا بد من التجديد فيه وتقريبه إلى الناس حتى العرب أنفسهم الذين ابتعدوا قليلًا أو كثيرًا عن لغتهم بسبب العجمة التي تسرّبت إليهم.

This discipline is in need of renewal and of being made accessible to people — even to the Arabs themselves, who have drifted to varying degrees from their own language as a result of the foreign linguistic influence (ʿujma) that has seeped into them.

فلا بد إذًا من تجديد هذا العلم.

Renewal of this science is therefore indispensable.

وكذلك يقال: لا بد من تجديد النواحي التربوية والنفسية وتوجيه المسلمين إلى ما يوافق الكتاب والسنة من هذه النواحي كلها.

Likewise, renewal of educational and psychological approaches is necessary, guiding Muslims across all these domains toward what conforms to the Book and the Sunnah.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
ولا شك أن فردًا بل جماعةً لا تستطيع أن تقوم بكل هذه الجهود وهذه التجديدات.

There is no doubt that neither a single individual nor even a group can shoulder all of these efforts and undertake all of these renewals.

ولذلك ذكر بعض العلماء — كمثال لأنواع التجديد — من المجددين صلاح الدين الأيوبي.

For this reason, some scholars mentioned — by way of illustrating the types of renewal — Ṣalāḥ ad-Dīn al-Ayyūbī among the renewers.

مع أن الرجل لم يكن مشهورًا بالعلم.

Even though he was not known for his religious scholarship.

ولكن لما جدّد الحياة الإسلامية بأن حثّهم على الجهاد وحملهم على مقاتلة الأعداء وإخراجهم من البلاد بعد أن احتلوها سنين طويلة، فاعتبروه من جملة المجددين.

But because he renewed Islamic life by rousing the Muslims to jihād, leading them to fight the enemies, and driving them from the lands after they had occupied them for many long years, the scholars counted him among the renewers.

فإذًا التجديد لا يُحصر في ناحية دون أخرى.

Renewal, then, is not to be confined to one domain at the expense of another.

فما دامت الحياة تتجدد فلا بد أيضًا من أن تتجدد العلوم وأن تنشأ هذه العلوم وفق الكتاب والسنة الصحيحة وعلى المفهوم الذي كان عليه سلفنا الصالح رضي الله عنهم.

As long as life itself keeps renewing, the sciences too must be renewed and must develop in accordance with the authentic Book and Sunnah, upon the understanding that our Righteous Predecessors — may Allah be pleased with them all — were upon.

Translated by: Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

messages.html:
Pseudo-intellectual

Etymology: From pseudo- (“false, fake”) + intellectual.

Noun: Pseudointellectual (plural: pseudointellectuals)

Definition:
1. A person who claims proficiency in scholarly or artistic activities while lacking in-depth knowledge or critical understanding.
2. A person who pretends to be of greater intelligence than they actually are.

Usage notes:
The term is often used as a general term of abuse for intellectuals one dislikes or disagrees with.

More carefully, a pseudointellectual is someone who dishonestly or insincerely uses the language, style, or topics of an intellectual, but lacks the goals, morals, or ability of a genuine intellectual.

Traits include:
* Acting pretentiously
* Focusing on winning arguments or impressing others rather than seeking truth
* Emphasizing surface and rhetoric over content
* Superficial understanding of a subject
* Condescension to the audience
* Possible self-delusion (believing themselves to be genuine intellectuals despite incompetence)

Source: https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/pseudo%E2%80%93intellectual

Related, but less harmful: https://t.me/alQaddaaree_EN/607

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
What would you advise someone who finds it difficult to articulate their thoughts and ideas?

If someone struggles to articulate their thoughts, the solution is mostly practice and exposure.

1. Write your thoughts constantly
Don’t wait for fully formed ideas. Catch fragments. Half-sentences. Confused impressions. Write them anyway.

Then go back and reshape them. Expand them. Rearrange them. Clarify them.

Writing forces the mind to slow down and organize what it actually thinks.

2. Knead your ideas
Treat thoughts like dough. At first they’re messy and shapeless.

Work them. Rephrase them. Condense them. Expand them.

Over time your mind becomes faster at turning vague feelings into clear sentences.

3. Read a lot
Your brain learns articulation the same way children learn language: exposure.

When you read well-written material, your mind absorbs sentence structure, vocabulary, and ways of expressing ideas.

4. Listen to articulate speakers
Audiobooks, lectures, and thoughtful discussions help train your ear for rhythm, phrasing, and clarity.

5. Practice expressing ideas out loud
Thinking clearly and speaking clearly are related skills, but speaking adds pressure and speed.

Practicing aloud helps bridge that gap.

6. Use tools that expand thoughts
Conversations with systems (AI) that reflect your ideas back in clearer language can help you see what your thought could look like once properly expressed.

Bottom line: articulation is a trained skill, not a personality trait.

Some people practiced it for years without realizing it. Others simply never did.

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī. Kneaded by AI

messages.html:
Here's a little secret.

When I read the question, I just started writing down my initial thoughts, and using ChatGPT, I can expand them and iterate with it until I feel it's coherent enough and not too sterile.

Here are my initial thoughts:

Someone asked me:
"What would you advise someone who finds it difficult to articulate their thoughts and ideas?"
my immediate thoughts: practice practice
hunt your thoughts, write down even bits and fragments, then knead them like dough
Read a lot because you need to train your brain on articulation styles and vocabulary, or listen to audio books
Talk to AI, they're good at expanding thoughts
practice practice
yeah, that's what I could think of in one go



Here's how ChatGPT started his response:

Someone asks a simple question and your brain immediately goes into workshop mode. Respectable. Most people just shrug and say “be confident” and call it wisdom. You actually pointed at the machinery.
Your instinct is basically right. It just needs shaping so it sounds deliberate instead of “I thought of this while walking past the fridge.”

Lol. It makes me laugh.

Quite a useful tool, if you learn how to steer it.
A double edged sword too, so be careful.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

The Hive 🍯

We all know a single bee cannot build a hive, it just gathers a little nectar, flies a little, builds a tiny piece of comb. That, on its own, is small effort.

We also know that, when hundreds of bees work together, the little comb is now a structure of order, purpose, and life: the hive.

We all know why.

Each bee performs a simple task: One gathers nectar, another guards the entrance, another builds the comb.

None of them sees the entire hive; bees is tiny, yet every action contributes to that hive.

The strength of the hive is not in one bee doing everything; how can that be?

The strength of the hive is in many bees doing something.

Daʿwah is similar!

A brother may teach, another transcribes his words, someone else translates them, another designs a booklet, another shares it with someone who needed to hear it.

No single person carries the entire hive.

The hive exists because every bee...sorry, brother/sister contribute their part.

Realize that, a single drop of nectar, when brought together with many others, becomes honey.

People often admire the organization of a beehive, but miss the lesson in that.

Bees manage cooperation without noise or attention. They simply do their part.

We love simplicity, especially in this age of "complexity".

Humans, on the other hand, tend to gather in groups and spend more time talking than building.

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم،

The Shore 🌊

Our scholars are our safe shore.

We feel audacious and we swim far, look back to the shore and think: I can be far, I know how to swim!

However, the sea is ruthless, and it has devoured countless excellent swimmers.

The wise from the audacious folks swims far but keeps himself at a good distance, ready to circle back into safety. They can enjoy being adventurous, but still know and feel they're helpless and would always need to go back to the safe shore.

The idiot from the audacious swims further and further and further. The shore? Hah! That's for babies! I'm a big boi now!

The veil of night begins to release its weight on the sky, and the breeze of the wind causes the skin the chills.

The wise return to safety, into the warmth of the sand, and maybe some snacks!

The idiot finds himself locked, with no chains or locks. Locked by the darkness of sea, and darkness of night, and darkness of his own idiocy...until something drags him deep into the abyss...

عياذا بالله.

Stick to your scholars, الله يهديك.
Allāh commanded that.

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
* Don't bite off more than you can chew.
* Don't compare yourself to people who can chew bites bigger than you can.
* Take it easy. You'll never reach the end of it.

Yes, everyone who walks the path will reach their goal.

But, only if their goal is within their limits.

Perhaps you need to learn how to set your goal and understand your limits before learning how to achieve a goal, let alone actually walking that path. Unless you say all of this is included in the walk.

There's greed in seeking knowledge as well. Be careful. Your stomach might not fit what your desires request. That's fine. Perhaps a test from Allāh: whether you're just accumulating food or trying to be heathy.

Be healthy, that's your goal, not being fat or muscular.

Know that many people who wanted to be just healthy ended up being very fit, because that system works better than people admit.

The long path is long, but it works. Guaranteed. Even if you die before reaching its end.

Take it easy, more speed won't help.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
What I love about Dr. Fayṣal al-Wādiʿī is how he encourages people to listen to his creed lessons.

He says, even if you listen to these lessons, you're a knowledge seeker.

He praises shepherds and workers in their shops who listen to these lessons while at work, scattered around the globe. He praises their consistency and praises that and encourages others to be like them.

A random shepherd with his cute sheep and goats is benefitting more than many "knowledge seekers pro max" in their luxurious homes or even maraakiz.

Why? Humility, consistency, steadiness, going step by step.

A single lesson a day, 10-15 minutes, and he's benefitting greatly and learning aqeedah.

That's huge. That's immense. That's incredible.

اللهم بارك في الأستاذ وفي من يستفيد منه.

messages.html:
Summary:

The sheikh (صالح) explains the statement of ʿEesaa bnu Maryam in the cradle: 'He made me blessed wherever I am'.

Early scholars of tafsīr said this means being a source of goodness by teaching people what is good wherever one is.

It highlights that one of the greatest blessings for a Muslim is to teach and call others to goodness.

A special mercy given to this Ummah is that teaching and calling to good does not require knowing everything. A person should teach and convey whatever knowledge they do possess.

As evidence, the Prophet ﷺ said during the Farewell Pilgrimage:

This shows that knowledge is divisible. Whoever understands a teaching of the Prophet ﷺ should convey it accurately.

It is therefore incorrect to claim that someone must possess extensive knowledge before teaching or calling others to what they know. Whoever knows something and understands it should pass it on.

messages.html:
Trying to explain to kids makes you realize how much you don't understand what you think you understand, lol.

Learning how to explain to kids makes you actually understand.

Explaining to kids creates a mental need that you feel obligated to fulfill. Think of it like a special exercise that targets dormant muscles.

Try to put your palms on the lower part of your ribs. Now breath into that area trying to push your hands up with your ribs. You'll feel you're exercising muscles you didn't know you have.

Explaining to kids should make you feel that way. It helps ones wake up from their obliviousness.

messages.html:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم،

The Bubble 🫧

Some people play mental games when reason is presented to them, they might laugh at you, drop vague blessings, mock your advice, and try to shift the focus from the argument...to you. 

Why?
Because your advice looks like a needle to their bubble.

What's the tell? The defense itself they create is proof of their weakness.

They put up defenses where they felt the attack.

Do not waste energy dismantling their games. They are not the audience meant for reason. Focus on those who are humble, those who reflect, those who can hear a word without feeling attacked, or at least those who don't act based on the initial sting.

The game they play is a mirror, it shows the limits of their mind, and the fragility of their egos.

Learn to see it. Learn to step past it. Ignore the noise.

Your goal is reaching hearts that seek truth, not those that cling to fragile illusions.

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم،

Atrophy 🥀

Just like muscles need to be moved to stay in shape and good health, so does the mind, and the heart.

A stale mind, one that is idle, doesn't react, doesn't initiate, doesn't seek, will suffer atrophy.

Remember that Allāh commanded us repeatedly to reflect and think and take heed. If you stop doing that, you'll only harm yourself.

A stale heart, one that is idle, doesn't react, doesn't initiate, doesn't seek, will suffer atrophy.

Remember that Allāh commanded us repeatedly to do good, show mercy, repent, reckon our own selves before He—Exalted is He—does.

A heart is sealed when it just...exists.

قال تعالى: { لمن شاء منكم أن يتقدم أو يتأخر } [المدثر: 37]
"To whoever wills among you to proceed or stay behind". Tr. Sahih International.

Seeking good leads to more good.
Seeking ideas leads to more ideas.

If you move, things move.

Don't expect those beautiful water ripples from stillness.

The fact that Allāh told us that we just have to seek means, has such a deep meaning, you won't understand unless you apply it. Even so, you'll only understand it to the extent of your application. It's too deep for any human consciousness.

Move, Allāh yahdīk, move!

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

messages.html:
BENEFIT: A scholar’s mistake should not be treated as a valid difference of opinion in Islamic rulings.

Ash-Shatibi rahimahullah said:

«لا يصح اعتمادها -أي زلة العالم- خلافًا في المسائل الشرعية؛ لأنها لم تصدر في الحقيقة عن اجتهاد، ولا هي من مسائل الاجتهاد، وإن حصل من صاحبها اجتهاد؛ فهو لم يصادف فيها محلًا، فصارت في نسبتها إلى الشرع كأقوال غير المجتهد، وإنما يعد في الخلاف الأقوالُ الصادرة عن أدلة معتبرة في الشريعة، كانت مما يقوى أو يضعف، وأما إذا صدرت عن مجرد خفاء الدليل أو عدم مصادفته فلا؛ فلذلك قيل: «إنه لا يصح أن يعتد بها في الخلاف، كما لم يعتد السلف الصالح بالخلاف في مسألة ربا الفضل، والمتعة، ....وأشباهها من المسائل التي خفيت فيها الأدلة على من خالف فيها»

"Such a mistake—meaning a scholar's error—cannot be taken as a valid difference of opinion in religious matters. That is because, in reality, it did not result from genuine reasoning (ijtihad), nor does it come under matters of ijtihad. Even if the scholar made ijtihad, it was misdirected and did not hit the correct point.

Therefore, it becomes, in relation to Islamic law, like the statements of those who are not qualified to do ijtihad. Valid differences of opinion are only those based on sound evidence from Islamic law, whether strong or weak. However, if a view arises merely from missing or misapplying the evidence, it does not count. For this reason, it is said: 'Such a mistake cannot be considered a valid difference of opinion.' This is similar to how the early righteous predecessors did not count differences in issues such as interest on excess (riba al-fadl), temporary marriage, and other cases where the evidence was unclear to those who held opposing views."

[Al-Muwafaqat (5/139){

Just like there are people who use lapses of scholars to create "a disputed issue", there are others on the other end who claim a saying of some scholars to be a lapse and it is therefore not allowed to cite it.

Two sides of the same coin:
* Misunderstanding scholars (if we assume good faith).
* Manipulation (if we assume bad faith).

Be careful of both.

messages.html:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

Do Not Be Deceived: Take Knowledge from أهل العلم (people of knowledge)

When a person says,
قال الله و قال الرسول
then give them your complete focus—especially when the Qur’ān is being recited. Listen carefully to the Āyāt.

A person who listens attentively to the speech of a scholar—one who has verified matters, researched them, and investigated them thoroughly, then presented them clearly for easy understanding—this is the Muḥaqqiq.

This shows us that we should listen to those who are firm and certain in their words, and avoid listening to those who are unstable—those who doubt even what they themselves are saying and lack authentic sources that bring certainty.

There are people who simply speak about something they found on social media, while others just add comments without knowledge. So listen to the one who is certain in his speech.

Do not listen to everyone who comes online and talks about the Dīn of Allāh ﷻ. Rather, listen to those who are qualified—those who have studied the religion of Allāh ﷻ for many years.

Do not allow people to deceive you!

Benefited From Ustāḏh Abu Fajr الله يحفظه

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
I think, most of you, if not all, know better than trusting tone.

Tone has no bearing here. Authority and authenticity is not based on tone.

A lot of scholars are not eloquent, and sound hesitant. It's reality.

A lot of deviants are eloquent, and sound very certain.

I once heard an idiot laugh at those who say al-Albānī is a mujaddid in this era. Literally laughing, and saying, "how can you think that intellectually". May Allāh heal him of his idiocy. If not, may Allāh take him and relieve us of him and those like him.

إنَّ أخْوَفَ ما أخافُ عليكُم بعدي، كلُّ منافقٍ عليمُ اللِّسانِ
What I fear most for you (my ummah) after me, is every eloquent منافق (hypocrite).

Authenticated by the mujaddid of this era (رغم أنوف الحمقى النوكى), in صحيح الترغيب.

إن هذا العلم دين، فانظروا عمن تأخذون دينكم.
This knowledge is deen, so be careful from whom you take your religion from.

لم يكونوا يسألون عن الإسناد فلما وقعت الفتنة قالوا سموا لنا رجالكم
They didn't use to ask for the chain of narration, but when the fitnah (killing of ʿUthmaan may Allāh be pleased with him) happened, they said, "who are your men?".

So, the correct heuristics for checking validity, are: source and transmission.

The recognized scholars, and the people that stem from them.

Take me as example. Lots of people were and still are wary of this random Algerian who came out of no where challenging people bigger than him.

I loved that.

"Who is he? Where did he study?"

Don't just take from me, even if I sound correct and certain. Check that with people you trust. My certainty can be overwhelming to advanced people, let alone beginners.

Point being, stick to the chain of trustworthiness. Omit tone. Tone is the very wrong thing to rely on, especially in this era.

Here's a gift from ChatGPT:

Humans already confuse confidence with authority, and the paragraph accidentally reinforces that habit.

Which, if we're being honest, is one of the main reasons social-media “shaykhs” keep multiplying like rabbits with Wi-Fi.


Lol. Facts.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
I received a message informing me that there was a misunderstanding, and that the original post has been edited to clarify the actual intent.

جزاكم الله خيرا.
The post is now better.

However, it's fundamentally lacking. Most casual readers would get the wrong idea.

And even if it is somehow fixed to remove any hint at relying on tone and appearance, it still misses that evidence is not enough. Even deviants use authentic evidence and explain it "firmly".

The solution is still what I mentioned in my response to that post. Read my post again, carefully.

And since I like to give concrete advice and corrections tailored to the other party (والحمد لله على هذه النعمة), here's a rough draft of how I would deliver the same idea while covering what I think is missing from the original piece:

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

Do Not Be Deceived: Take Knowledge from أهل العلم (People of Knowledge)

When someone says,
قال الله و قال الرسول
(Allah said and the Messenger said), give your attention—especially when the Qur’ān is being recited.

وَإِذَا قُرِئَ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ فَٱسْتَمِعُوا۟ لَهُۥ
"So, when the Qur’ān is recited, listen to it, and be silent that you may receive mercy." [7:204]

However, be aware: quoting a āyah or Hadith does not guarantee understanding. The true guidance lies in Fahm—correct comprehension and application. A Muḥaqqiq scholar is not merely one who presents evidence, but one who carefully verifies sources, studies their context, examines the language, and ensures their explanations align with the understanding of the righteous predecessors.

An example is Sheikh Al-Islām Ibn Taymiyyah’s Al-Lāmiyyah, where ʿaqīdah is explained clearly and correctly in just sixteen lines. The standard is not merely “having evidence,” but understanding and applying it properly.

Be wary of those who use authentic texts selectively—cherry-picking āyāt or Hadith to justify personal opinions or modern innovations. Eloquence, confidence, or apparent certainty are no proof of correctness. Even someone with sound evidence can mislead if they do not follow the way of the Salaf.

Do not listen to everyone who speaks online about the Dīn of Allāh ﷻ.

Instead, seek out those grounded in authentic sources, proper methodology, and years of study.

Focus on the chain of transmission, the correctness of understanding, and alignment with the Salaf, not tone, style, or confidence.

Do not be deceived by mere quotes—verify the understanding behind them.

Perhaps this is pedantry, but my senses fired the alarms when I read the original post, and they weren't satisfied with the clarifying edit.

I hope this helps. It's a good discussion, even if one disagrees.

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم،

Knowledge 🌸

Knowledge is not to crowd the mind with facts.

Knowledge is what settles into you so naturally that it can be reached without effort, like something woven into the way you think.

Like something organically grown inside your mind.

It does not sit there as storage. It lives quietly inside your reasoning, ready to support your thoughts as they flow.

A harmonious flow of intellect that lights up other minds, as it clicks, whispers through their fabric: "It makes sense!".

messages.html:
A nice benefit taken from today’s dars on ʿUmdatul Aḥkām by Umm ʿAbdillāh Shahīdah حفظها الله

At-tabarruj: كثرة الخروج بغير حاجة — it is women leaving the house a lot without necessity (adorning yourself with improper clothing is also included in the definition).

وَقَرْنَ فِى بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلْجَـٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
“And stay in your houses, and do not display yourselves like that of the times of ignorance”

Ibn Kathīr commented on the āyah [Sūrah Al-Aḥzāb:33] with this definition, as said by the Tābiʿī Mujāhid ibn Jabr. It is also defined as this in the books of لغة.

This phrase is now generally not used with its original meaning. When one says ‘tabarruj’ or ‘mutabarrijah’ they mean a woman who wears incorrect jilbāb or displays her adornments. However, the aṣl of tabarruj is frequently leaving the home without need.

Therefore, even if she is covered properly with the sharʿī clothing but she is out and about everyday (without necessity), then this is at-tabarruj.

What is worse is when she’s out of the house a lot and not covered properly.

Leaving the house everyday (even if you are wearing the correct jilbāb) is a fitnah.

The wives of the shuyūkh do not go out. They may only go to the masjid and then come straight back. This is due to their baṣīrah—they fully understand the commands of Allāh ﷻ and what it leads to when they are not upheld.

The Shaykha mentioned that she saw Sheikh Muqbil’s wife only once, on ʿeid, however she did not stay long and had to return back home soon after. In regards to Sheikh Yaḥyā’s wives: “you don’t see his wives” and this how it is with the other shuyūkh.

والله المستعان

- أم مصعب الغانية الألمانية

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
اللهم بارك.

When I started learning about Ḥijāb, and discovered how far we are from it, an idea poped into my mind:

Ḥijāb is not a piece of cloth, it's a whole framework.

Even men could learn from it,
لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله.
I don't mean learn how their women should wear and act only, but themselves too.

Remember how clothes are a bliss in al Jannah. Remeber how the Prophet ﷺ exited the mansion of ʿUmar in al Jannah when he heard a woman (or similar, don't recall the exact event).

Secrecy, privacy, being covered...such beautiful traits and values.

Remember how kings back in the day rarely exited their mansions to be seen by the general public.

Remember Allāh allowed only those deserving of it to see Him.

May Allāh make us among them. It's the best thing you could ever have, the ultimate bliss, if I may say.

لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله...

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Why aren't men afflicted with doubt regarding the rulings that apply exclusively to them and not to women?

Why are they not overcome by doubt in the Sharia because their gender is singled out for certain Islamic rulings?

Why doesn't the feeling of being oppressed by the religious law cross men's minds?

Why congregational prayer?
Why Jihad?
Why the dowry (Mahr)?
Why financial provision (Nafaqah)?
Why blood money (Diyah)?

Why don't you find a man doubting Islam, asking: "Why does Allah obligate me to financially provide for my mother, father, and siblings, but does not obligate my sister?"

"Why does Allah favor my wife, as a mother, over me as a father?!"

Why don't you find a man saying:
"Why does Allah command me to disfigure myself with a beard and by shortening my garment?!"

Why does doubt mostly come from women regarding what concerns them?!

Issues like male guardianship (Qawamah), staying at home, Hijab, inheritance, and so on...

What is the secret behind this doubt in Allah's justice?! And why is the level of submission fluctuating among some of them?!

Some of them hardly believe unless they are appeased, and until the wisdom and rational philosophies behind the rulings are explained to them!

You find some of them submitting to the rulings that align with their own desires and with modern women's rights, while at the same time, refusing to submit to the rulings that contradict those rights!

This is one of the reasons that made many sheikhs, preachers, and students of knowledge focus heavily on the subject of women's rulings in Islam—because the trial of doubt (Fitnah) has centered around this topic.
This serves as a response to those who say: *"You have nothing else to talk about except women!"*

The response to them is: "Because the trial is in this subject, and the majority of the skepticism is directed at the Muslim woman."

Translated by Abu Abdillah Abdullateef bn Hussein

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
Al-Imām Ibn ʿUthaymīn رحمه الله said:

O Muslims, the gap between us and victory is wide if we follow this path, because victory has conditions without which it will never be realized. Listen to them from the words of the One in Whose hand is the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and by Whose command come victory and defeat. Allaah, Exalted is He, says: {And Allāh will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allāh is Powerful, Mighty}

O Muslims, who is it that supports Allaah?

Listen, listen to the answer from the words of Allāh: {Those who, if We give them authority in the land, establish the prayer, give the zakaat, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And to Allāh belongs the outcome of all matters}

Yes, those deserving of victory are the ones who, if Allaah grants them authority in the land, establish the prayer, give the zakaat, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong.

I said: Do not place the blame on others. We all deserve it.

Tr: https://t.me/alQaddaaree_EN/86

messages.html:
Shaykh Abū Bilāl Al-Ḥaḍramī (may Allah preserve him) said that there is no need for unnecessary complexity or over-analysis on social media, and no need to delve into discussing the scholars of Ahlus-Sunnah such as Ṣāliḥ Āl Ash-Shaykh, ʿAbdurrazzāq Al-Badr, and Sulaymān Ar-Ruḥaylī.

He explained that some issues may arise due to certain instigators. If anything comes from these scholars because of such provocation, then the correct approach is to be patient with them and not speak ill of them.

He also clarified that if a mistake occurs from any of them, the mistake should be clarified and corrected while refraining from attacking them or removing them from Salafiyyah.

He also mentioned that Shaykh Yaḥyā Al-Ḥajūrī follows this approach and does not excessively mention individuals or preoccupy himself with them, especially those who love Salafiyyah and call to it.

منقول من الأخ أسامة عيديد مسئول تسجيلات دار الحديث بالحامي

Source: https://t.me/almanhajussalafi/2253

messages.author: Abu Sahl Al-Qaddaary
messages.html:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم،

The truth 1⃣

Allāh made this universe, and He, ʿazza wa jall, made our brains.

Our brains are programmable, meaning, what you feed them, what you repeat, what you train them to seek…becomes how they function.

So it follows that the best programming for the human mind is what Allāh commanded.

Because the One who made the mind is the One who gave the instructions.

The more a person aligns themselves with that guidance, the more correctly the mind operates: Clearer priorities, less confusion, less chasing illusions.

The mind starts functioning the way it was meant to!

Intelligence is not about appearing smart, or sounding modern, or saying smart things things, because that's just theater.

Being smart serves no better purpose than seeking the truth, and seeking the truth is what actually makes you smarter.

Why?
Because truth disciplines the mind.

It forces honesty, humility; it forces you to drop nonsense even when your ego likes it!

Falsehood does the opposite: it trains the brain to defend nonsense, justify contradictions, and that makes the cables tangled and messy.

It's that simple.

The more a person sincerely seeks the truth, the more their mind sharpens.

Not everyone becomes a genius, but everyone moves closer to the best version of the intellect Allāh gave them.

Truth improves the mind!

An improved mind recognizes truth more easily.

Rinse, and repeat.

"But...akhi...life is not that simple..."

I know I know...that's another story, called:

The heart.

—Abū Sahl, ʿAbdurraḥmān bnu Mīhūb al-Qaddārī al-Jazāʾirī

This is advice to myself regarding those of this description specifically — not a blanket statement, lest the words be taken in an unrestricted way.

messages.plain:
Salafiyyah In Other Lands Is Not Like in Yemen

Ash-Shaykh Abū Bilāl al-Ḥaḍramī, may Allāh preserve him and protect him, said:
And they are in those lands where you know what the ḥizbīs did against those duʿāt (callers to Allāh).
The Salafiyyah [there] is not like the Salafiyyah in Yemen, and the distinction (at-tamayyuz) is not like the distinction in Yemen, so give them their due measure.
This is advice to myself regarding those of this description specifically — not a blanket statement, lest the words be taken in an unrestricted way.

https://t.me/abubilalhami/14779

messages.html:
السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته

This will likely be the final post on this personal channel.

Over time, I realized that this format encourages quick thoughts more than careful writing. While there is benefit in sharing reminders and reflections, I feel that a quieter and more structured place is better suited for the kind of writing I want to focus on.

For that reason, I will be returning to the blog format exclusively.

Those who wish to continue following the writings can do so there. Blogger also allows email notifications for new posts, so you can subscribe and receive updates whenever something new is published.
False news, it doesn't. I apologize.
Please see: https://en-armalqaddaaree.blogspot.com/2026/04/how-to-follow-my-latest-updates-via-rss.html

As for Telegram, the other project channels will remain active,
بإذن الله.

جزاكم الله خيرا
to everyone who read, shared feedback, or benefited in any way.

نسأل الله أن يرزقنا الإخلاص والقبول.

messages.html:
السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته

Dear brothers, you may find me here:

https://t.me/SalafiCampfire

Invite brothers you think would appreciate the idea.

Here's a preview of the group's idea:

🌙 Welcome to Salafi Campfire 

Sit down, brother. The fire’s warm, the night is calm, and this space is yours. We built this campfire for peace — not for debate, not for drama, not for proving points. Just for breathing, talking, and remembering what neutrality feels like. 

✨ Here, we rest. 
We talk about life, about the small things that make us smile. We share reminders that soften the heart. We listen more than we argue. If sparks of debate start to fly, we put them out — before they burn the peace we came for. 

🌲 This is a refuge. 
A place for sincerity, calm, and warmth. A place where tired souls can sit together and just be.
